units.zh: 高仙芝，本高麗人也。
units.en: Gao Xianzhi was ethnically Korean.
units.literal: Gao Xianzhi was originally a man of Koguryo.

units.zh: 父舍雞，初從河西軍，累勞至四鎮十將、諸衛將軍。
units.en: His father Sheji had first served with the Hexi armies and, through long service, rose to become a Ten-General of the Four Garrisons and a palace guard general.
units.literal: His father Sheji at first followed the Hexi army; through accumulated labors he rose to Ten-General of the Four Garrisons and a general of the Palace Guards.

units.zh: 仙芝美姿容，善騎射，勇決驍果。
units.en: Xianzhi was handsome, an expert horseman and archer, and bold, decisive, and ferocious in battle.
units.literal: Xianzhi had a handsome appearance, was skilled at mounted archery, and was brave, resolute, fierce, and daring.

units.zh: 少隨父至安西，以父有功授遊擊將軍。
units.en: As a young man he accompanied his father to Anxi and, thanks to his father's service record, was granted the rank of General of Resist-the-Enemy.
units.literal: In youth he followed his father to Anxi; because of his father's merit he was appointed General of Resist-the-Enemy.

units.zh: 年二十餘即拜將軍，與父同班秩。
units.en: By his twenties he already held general's rank, equal in grade to his father.
units.literal: Before he was twenty-some years old he was already appointed as a general, sharing rank with his father.

units.zh: 事節度使田仁琬、蓋嘉運，未甚任用，後夫蒙靈察累拔擢之。
units.en: Under commissioners Tian Renwan and Gai Jiayun he saw little use; Fumeng Lingcha later promoted him again and again.
units.literal: He served under Military Commissioners Tian Renwan and Gai Jiayun and was not much employed; afterward Fumeng Lingcha repeatedly promoted and advanced him.

units.zh: 開元末，為安西副都護、四鎮都知兵馬使。
units.en: Near the end of the Kaiyuan reign he was made Deputy Protector of Anxi and overall commander of the Four Garrisons' forces.
units.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he became Deputy Protector-General of Anxi and Commander-in-Chief of the Military Forces of the Four Garrisons.

units.zh: 小勃律國王為吐蕃所招，妻以公主，西北二十餘國皆為吐蕃所制，貢獻不通。
units.en: The king of Lesser Bolü had been won over by Tibet, which married a princess to him; more than twenty kingdoms in the northwest fell under Tibetan control, and tribute routes were cut off.
units.literal: The king of Lesser Bolü was enticed by Tibet, which gave him a princess as wife; more than twenty states of the northwest were all controlled by Tibet, so tribute could not get through.

units.zh: 後節度使田仁琬、蓋嘉運並靈察累討之，不捷，玄宗特敕仙芝以馬步萬人為行營節度使往討之。
units.en: Commissioners Tian, Gai, and Lingcha had campaigned against them repeatedly without victory; the emperor then appointed Xianzhi Mobile-Camp Commissioner with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to lead the punitive expedition.
units.literal: Later Military Commissioners Tian Renwan, Gai Jiayun, and Lingcha repeatedly attacked them without success; Xuanzong specially ordered Xianzhi, with ten thousand horse and foot, to serve as Mobile-Camp Military Commissioner and go punish them.

units.zh: 時步軍皆有私馬，自安西行十五日至撥換城，又十餘日至握瑟德，又十餘日至疏勒，又二十餘日至蔥嶺守捉，又行二十餘日至播密川，又二十餘日至特勒滿川，即五識匿國也。
units.en: The foot soldiers all brought their own mounts. From Anxi it was a fifteen-day march to Baraghan, then another ten-odd days to Wusede, another ten-odd to Kashgar, more than twenty to the Congling garrison, another twenty-odd to the Bomichuan, and another twenty-odd to Telmanchuan — the territory of the Five Shi kingdoms.
units.literal: At that time the infantry all had private horses. From Anxi it was fifteen days to Baraghan City, then more than ten days to Wusede, then more than ten days to Kashgar, then more than twenty days to the Congling frontier garrison, then another twenty-odd days to Bomichuan, then another twenty-odd days to Telmanchuan — which was the land of the Five Shi kingdoms.

units.zh: 仙芝乃分為三軍：使疏勒守捉使趙崇玭統三千騎趣吐蕃連雲堡，自北谷入；
units.en: Xianzhi split his army three ways: he sent the Kashgar commissioner Zhao Chongpin with three thousand horsemen against the Tibetan stronghold at Lianyunbao by the northern valley;
units.literal: Xianzhi then divided his forces into three armies: he sent the Kashgar frontier commissioner Zhao Chongpin to command three thousand cavalry toward the Tibetan fortress of Lianyunbao, entering by the northern valley;

units.zh: 使撥換守捉使賈崇瓘自赤佛堂路入；
units.en: the Baraghan commissioner Jia Chongguan by the Chifotang road;
units.literal: he sent the Baraghan frontier commissioner Jia Chongguan to enter by the Chifotang route;

units.zh: 仙芝與中使邊令誠自護密國入，約七月十三日辰時會於吐蕃連雲堡。
units.en: and he himself, with the palace envoy Bian Lingcheng, entered from Humi, all three columns to converge at Lianyunbao at the chen hour on the thirteenth of the seventh month.
units.literal: and Xianzhi with the palace envoy Bian Lingcheng entered from the kingdom of Humi, arranging to meet at the Tibetan Lianyunbao at the chen hour on the thirteenth day of the seventh month.

units.zh: 堡中有兵千人，又城南十五里因山為柵，有兵八九千人。
units.en: The fort held a thousand men, and fifteen li to the south a mountain stockade held eight or nine thousand more.
units.literal: In the fortress were a thousand troops; fifteen li south of the city, relying on the mountains, a stockade had been built with eight or nine thousand troops.

units.zh: 城下有婆勒川，水漲不可渡。
units.en: Below the walls ran the Bole River, now in flood and impassable.
units.literal: Below the city was the Bole River; the water had risen and could not be crossed.

units.zh: 仙芝以三牲祭河，命諸將選兵馬，人賫三日幹糧，早集河次。
units.en: Xianzhi sacrificed to the river, ordered his commanders to pick their men and mounts, issued three days' rations to each soldier, and had them muster at the river at dawn.
units.literal: Xianzhi offered the three sacrificial animals to the river and ordered the generals to select troops and horses; each man was to carry three days' dry rations and assemble early at the riverbank.

units.zh: 水既難渡，將士皆以為狂。
units.en: With the river so swollen, the troops thought him mad.
units.literal: Since the water was hard to cross, officers and soldiers all thought it madness.

units.zh: 既至，人不濕旗，馬不濕韉，已濟而成列矣。
units.en: When they reached the bank, neither banner nor saddle was wet: they had already crossed and were drawn up in line.
units.literal: When they arrived, men's flags were not wet, horses' saddles were not wet — they had already crossed and were in formation.

units.zh: 仙芝喜謂令誠曰：「向吾半渡賊來，吾屬敗矣，今既濟成列，是天以此賊賜我也。」
units.en: Xianzhi said happily to Lingcheng, "Had the enemy struck while we were midstream, we were lost; now that we are across and formed up, Heaven has delivered these foes into my hands."
units.literal: Xianzhi said joyfully to Lingcheng: "If earlier, when we were half across, the enemy had come, we would have been defeated; now that we have crossed and are in formation, Heaven is giving me these enemies."

units.zh: 遂登山挑擊，從辰至巳，大破之。
units.en: He then stormed the heights and, fighting from the chen hour until si, routed them completely.
units.literal: He then climbed the mountain and attacked; from the chen hour to the si hour he inflicted a great defeat.

units.zh: 至夜奔逐，殺五千人，生擒千人，餘並走散。
units.en: He pursued through the night, killing five thousand, taking a thousand prisoners, and driving the rest to flight.
units.literal: By night he pursued in flight, killing five thousand men, capturing a thousand alive; the rest all scattered and fled.

units.zh: 得馬千餘匹，軍資器械不可勝數。
units.en: He seized more than a thousand horses and booty beyond reckoning.
units.literal: He obtained more than a thousand horses; military supplies and weapons were beyond counting.

units.zh: 玄宗使術士韓履冰往視日，懼不欲行，邊令誠亦懼。
units.en: The emperor had sent the diviner Han Lübing to observe the sun; Lübing feared and did not wish to go on, and Bian Lingcheng also feared.
units.literal: Xuanzong sent the diviner Han Lübing to observe the sun; [Xianzhi] feared and did not wish to go on, and Bian Lingcheng also feared.

units.zh: 仙芝留令誠等以羸病尪弱三千餘人守其城，仙芝遂進。
units.en: Xianzhi left Lingcheng with three thousand sick and weak men to hold the fort and pressed on.
units.literal: Xianzhi left Lingcheng and others with more than three thousand sick, weak, and feeble men to guard the city, and Xianzhi then advanced.

units.zh: 三日，至坦駒嶺，直下峭峻四十餘里，仙芝料之曰：「阿弩越胡若速迎，即是好心。」
units.en: On the third day they came to Tanjuling, where the trail dropped sheer for forty li. Xianzhi reasoned, "If the Anüyue tribesmen meet us promptly, their hearts are with us."
units.literal: On the third day they reached Tanjuling; straight down was a precipice of more than forty li. Xianzhi reckoned and said: "If the Anüyue barbarians welcome us quickly, that shows good intent."

units.zh: 又恐兵士不下，乃先令二十餘騎詐作阿弩越城胡服上嶺來迎。
units.en: Fearing his men would refuse the descent, he sent ahead twenty horsemen disguised as Anüyue tribesmen to ride down and welcome the army.
units.literal: He also feared the soldiers would not go down, so he first sent more than twenty horsemen disguised in Anüyue-city barbarian dress up the ridge to come welcome them.

units.zh: 既至坦駒嶺，兵士果不肯下，云：「大使將我欲何處去？」
units.en: At Tanjuling the troops would not budge. "Commissioner," they cried, "where are you leading us?"
units.literal: When they reached Tanjuling, the soldiers indeed would not go down, saying: "Commissioner, where are you taking us?"

units.zh: 言未畢，其先使二十人來迎，云：「阿弩越城胡並好心奉迎，娑夷河藤橋已斫訖。」
units.en: Before he could answer, his twenty scouts rode up, calling, "The Anüyue are ready to receive you — the vine bridge over the Suoyi has been cut down."
units.literal: Before the words were finished, the twenty men he had sent ahead came to welcome them, saying: "The Anüyue-city barbarians all welcome you in good faith; the vine bridge over the Suoyi River has already been cut."

units.zh: 仙芝陽喜以號令，兵士盡下。
units.en: Xianzhi pretended delight and gave the order; the men all descended.
units.literal: Xianzhi feigned joy and gave the order; the soldiers all went down.

units.zh: 娑夷河，即古之弱水也，不勝草芥毛發。
units.en: The Suoyi was the ancient Weak Water, which would not bear even a blade of grass or a strand of hair.
units.literal: The Suoyi River was the ancient Weak Water; it would not bear a blade of grass or a hair.

units.zh: 下嶺三日，越胡果來迎。
units.en: Three days below the pass, the Yue tribesmen did come out to meet them.
units.literal: Three days after descending the ridge, the Yue barbarians indeed came to welcome them.

units.zh: 明日，至阿弩越城，當日令將軍席元慶、賀婁餘潤先修橋路。
units.en: The next day they reached Anüyue City, and that same day he sent Generals Xi Yuanqing and Helou Yurun ahead to repair the bridge and road.
units.literal: The next day they reached Anüyue City; that same day he ordered Generals Xi Yuanqing and Helou Yurun to repair the bridge and road first.

units.zh: 仙芝明日進軍，又令元慶以一千騎先謂小勃律王曰：「不取汝城，亦不斫汝橋，但借汝路過，向大勃律去。」
units.en: The following day Xianzhi marched on and sent Yuanqing ahead with a thousand horsemen to tell the king of Lesser Bolü, "We do not mean to seize your city or destroy your bridge — we ask only passage on our way to Greater Bolü."
units.literal: The next day Xianzhi advanced the army and again ordered Yuanqing with a thousand cavalry to go ahead and tell the king of Lesser Bolü: "We will not take your city, nor will we cut your bridge — we only borrow passage through your land on the way to Greater Bolü."

units.zh: 城中有首領五六人，皆赤心為吐蕃。
units.en: Five or six chieftains in the city were wholly devoted to Tibet.
units.literal: In the city were five or six chieftains, all wholeheartedly serving Tibet.

units.zh: 仙芝先約元慶云：「軍到，首領百姓必走入山谷，招呼取以敕命賜彩物等，首領至，齊縛之以待我。」
units.en: Xianzhi had told Yuanqing beforehand, "When we arrive the chiefs and people will flee into the hills. Summon them with imperial gifts; when they come, bind them all and hold them for me."
units.literal: Xianzhi had beforehand agreed with Yuanqing: "When the army arrives, the chieftains and common people will surely flee into the valleys; summon them with imperial orders and gifts of colored goods and the like; when the chieftains come, bind them all together and wait for me."

units.zh: 元慶既至，一如仙芝之所教，縛諸首領。
units.en: Yuanqing did exactly as instructed and seized the chieftains.
units.literal: When Yuanqing arrived, just as Xianzhi had instructed, he bound all the chieftains.

units.zh: 王及公主走入石窟，取不可得。
units.en: The king and princess escaped into a cave and could not be captured.
units.literal: The king and princess fled into a stone cave and could not be taken.

units.zh: 仙芝至，斬其為吐蕃者五六人。
units.en: When Xianzhi arrived, he executed five or six of the Tibetan loyalists.
units.literal: When Xianzhi arrived, he beheaded five or six of those who served Tibet.

units.zh: 急令元慶斫藤橋，去勃律猶六十里，及暮，才斫了，吐蕃兵馬大至，已無及矣。
units.en: He ordered Yuanqing to cut the vine bridge at once. Bolü still lay sixty li away; the bridge was severed only at dusk, and Tibetan forces were already pouring in — too late to stop them.
units.literal: He urgently ordered Yuanqing to cut the vine bridge; Bolü was still sixty li away, and by evening it was only just cut down when Tibetan troops and horses arrived in great numbers — it was already too late.

units.zh: 藤橋闊一箭道，修之一年方成。
units.en: The vine bridge spanned no more than an arrow's shot and had taken a year to build.
units.literal: The vine bridge was as wide as an arrow's flight; it took a year to complete its repair.

units.zh: 勃律先為吐蕃所詐借路，遂成此橋。
units.en: Bolü had been tricked into letting Tibet use its roads, and the bridge had been built for that purpose.
units.literal: Bolü had earlier been tricked by Tibet into lending a route, and thus this bridge had been built.

units.zh: 至是，仙芝徐自招諭勃律及公主出降，並平其國。
units.en: Thereupon Xianzhi patiently persuaded the king of Bolü and the princess to surrender and pacified the kingdom.
units.literal: At this point Xianzhi gradually persuaded Bolü and the princess to come out and surrender, and pacified the state altogether.

units.zh: 天寶六載八月，仙芝虜勃律王及公主趣赤佛堂路班師。
units.en: In the eighth month of Tianbao 6, Xianzhi took the king of Bolü and the princess captive and withdrew by the Chifotang road.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year of Tianbao, Xianzhi took captive the king of Bolü and the princess and withdrew the army by the Chifotang route.

units.zh: 九月，復至婆勒川連雲堡，與邊令誠等相見。
units.en: In the ninth month they returned to Lianyunbao on the Bole River and met Bian Lingcheng and the others.
units.literal: In the ninth month they again reached Lianyunbao on the Bole River and met Bian Lingcheng and the others.

units.zh: 其月末，還播密川，令劉單草告捷書，遣中使判官王廷芳告捷。
units.en: At month's end they were back at Bomichuan; Xianzhi had Liu Dan draft the victory memorial and sent the palace envoy Wang Tingfang to court with the news.
units.literal: At month's end they returned to Bomichuan; he ordered Liu Dan to draft the victory report and sent the palace envoy and judge Wang Tingfang to announce the victory.

units.zh: 仙芝軍還至河西，夫蒙靈察都不使人迎勞，罵仙芝曰：「啖狗腸高麗奴！
units.en: When the army reached Hexi, Fumeng Lingcha sent no envoy to welcome them and cursed Xianzhi: "Korean cur who eats dog guts!
units.literal: When Xianzhi's army returned to Hexi, Fumeng Lingcha sent no one to welcome or comfort them; he cursed Xianzhi, saying: "Dog-gut-eating Korean slave!

units.zh: 啖狗屎高麗奴！
units.en: Korean cur who eats dog shit!
units.literal: Dog-shit-eating Korean slave!

units.zh: 於闐使誰與汝奏得？」
units.en: Who got you your posting as commissioner of Khotan?"
units.literal: Who petitioned on your behalf to get you the Khotan commissioner's post?"

units.zh: 仙芝曰：「中丞。」
units.en: Xianzhi said, "You did, Vice Commissioner."
units.literal: Xianzhi said: "The Vice Commissioner."

units.zh: 「焉耆鎮守使誰邊得？」
units.en: "And who got you the Yanqi garrison?"
units.literal: "Who got you the post of garrison commander of Yanqi on the frontier?"

units.zh: 曰：「中丞。」
units.en: He said, "You did, Vice Commissioner."
units.literal: He said: "The Vice Commissioner."

units.zh: 「安西副都護使誰邊得？」
units.en: "And the deputy protectorship of Anxi?"
units.literal: "Who got you the post of Deputy Protector-General of Anxi on the frontier?"

units.zh: 曰：「中丞。」
units.en: He said, "You did, Vice Commissioner."
units.literal: He said: "The Vice Commissioner."

units.zh: 「安西都知兵馬使誰邊得？」
units.en: "And command of Anxi's armies?"
units.literal: "Who got you the post of Commander-in-Chief of Anxi military forces on the frontier?"

units.zh: 曰：「中丞。」
units.en: He said, "You did, Vice Commissioner."
units.literal: He said: "The Vice Commissioner."

units.zh: 靈察曰：「此既皆我所奏，安得不待我處分懸奏捷書！
units.en: Lingcha said, "Since I recommended you for every one of these posts, how dare you send in a victory report without waiting for my approval!
units.literal: Lingcha said: "Since I petitioned for all of these, how could you not wait for my disposition before submitting the victory report on your own!

units.zh: 據高麗奴此罪，合當斬，但緣新立大功，不欲處置。」
units.en: For this the Korean wretch deserves death, but since he has just won a great victory I will let it pass."
units.literal: On this offense the Korean slave deserves execution, but because he has just achieved a great merit, I do not wish to punish him."

units.zh: 又謂劉單曰：「聞爾能作捷書。」
units.en: He turned to Liu Dan. "I hear you can draft victory memorials."
units.literal: He also said to Liu Dan: "I hear you can write victory reports."

units.zh: 單恐懼請罪。
units.en: Dan pleaded for mercy in terror.
units.literal: Dan, in fear, begged forgiveness.

units.zh: 令誠具奏其狀曰：「仙芝立奇功，今將憂死。」
units.en: Lingcheng reported the whole affair to court: "Xianzhi has won a signal victory and now fears for his life."
units.literal: Lingcheng submitted a full report of the situation, saying: "Xianzhi has achieved a singular merit, yet now faces death in anxiety."

units.zh: 其年六月，制授仙芝鴻臚卿、攝御史中丞，代夫蒙靈察為四鎮節度使，征靈察入朝。
units.en: That sixth month an edict made Xianzhi Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting censor-in-chief, replaced Lingcha as commissioner of the Four Garrisons, and recalled Lingcha to the capital.
units.literal: In the sixth month of that year an edict appointed Xianzhi Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Censor-in-Chief, replacing Fumeng Lingcha as Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons and summoning Lingcha to court.

units.zh: 靈察大懼，仙芝每日見之，趨走如故，靈察益不自安。
units.en: Lingcha was terrified; Xianzhi still called on him daily and waited on him as before, which only deepened Lingcha's unease.
units.literal: Lingcha was greatly afraid; Xianzhi saw him every day and hurried to attend as before, so Lingcha grew ever more ill at ease.

units.zh: 將軍程千里時為副都護，大將軍畢思琛為靈察押衙，行官王滔、康懷順、陳奉忠等，嘗構譖仙芝於靈察。
units.en: General Cheng Qianli was deputy protector; Grand General Bi Sichen was Lingcha's chief adjutant; and staff officers Wang Tao, Kang Huaishun, and Chen Fengzhong had once slandered Xianzhi to Lingcha.
units.literal: General Cheng Qianli was then Deputy Protector; Grand General Bi Sichen was Lingcha's yaya; staff officers Wang Tao, Kang Huaishun, Chen Fengzhong, and others had once slandered Xianzhi to Lingcha.

units.zh: 仙芝既領節度事，謂程千里曰：「公面似男兒，心如婦人，何也？」
units.en: Once in command, Xianzhi said to Cheng Qianli, "You have a man's face but a woman's heart — why is that?"
units.literal: After Xianzhi took charge of the commissioner's affairs, he said to Cheng Qianli: "Sir, your face is like a man's, but your heart is like a woman's — why?"

units.zh: 又謂思琛曰：「此胡敢來！
units.en: He said to Sichen, "This barbarian dares show his face here!
units.literal: He also said to Sichen: "This barbarian dares to come!

units.zh: 我城東一千石種子莊被汝將去，憶之乎？」
units.en: You seized my thousand-shi seed estate east of the city — do you remember?"
units.literal: The thousand-shi seed estate east of my city was taken away by you — do you remember?"

units.zh: 對曰：「此是中丞知思琛辛苦見乞。」
units.en: Sichen answered, "The Vice Commissioner knew my hardships and granted it at my plea."
units.literal: He replied: "This was because the Vice Commissioner knew Sichen's hardships and granted it on request."

units.zh: 仙芝曰：「吾此時懼汝作威福，豈是憐汝與之！
units.en: Xianzhi said, "I gave it to you then because I feared you would abuse your power — not out of pity!
units.literal: Xianzhi said: "At that time I feared you would wield power for yourself — how was it pity that made me give it to you!

units.zh: 我欲不言，恐汝懷憂，言了無事矣。」
units.en: I kept silent lest you worry; now that I have said it, let there be no trouble between us."
units.literal: I wanted not to speak, fearing you would brood in worry; now that I have spoken, there is no further matter."

units.zh: 又呼王滔等至，捽下將笞，良久皆釋之，由是軍情不懼。
units.en: He summoned Wang Tao and the others, had them thrown down for a beating, then after a long while released them — and from that the troops ceased to fear him.
units.literal: He also summoned Wang Tao and the others, threw them down and was about to flog them, but after a long while released them all; from this the army's morale was unafraid.

units.zh: 八載，入朝，加特進，兼左金吾衛大將軍同正員，仍與一子五品官。
units.en: In the eighth year he came to court, was granted special advancement, made grand general of the Left Golden Crow Guard, and given a fifth-rank post for one son.
units.literal: In the eighth year he entered court; he was given the special advancement rank and concurrently made Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard with regular appointment, and one son was granted a fifth-rank office.

units.zh: 九載，將兵討石國，平之，獲其國王以歸。
units.en: In the ninth year he campaigned against Shi, conquered it, and returned with its king as prisoner.
units.literal: In the ninth year he led troops to attack the state of Shi, pacified it, and brought back its king captive.

units.zh: 仙芝性貪，獲石國大塊瑟瑟十餘石、真金五六馲駝、名馬寶玉稱是。
units.en: Xianzhi was greedy; he took from Shi more than ten great blocks of kingfisher stone, five or six camel-loads of gold, and famous horses and jades beyond count.
units.literal: Xianzhi was greedy by nature; from Shi he obtained more than ten large lumps of se-se gemstone, five or six camels' loads of pure gold, and famous horses and precious jades in abundance.

units.zh: 初，舍雞以仙芝為懦緩，恐其不能自存，至是立功，家財鉅萬，頗能散施，人有所求，言無不應。
units.en: Sheji had once thought Xianzhi too timid to make his way; now, after his victories, his wealth ran to tens of thousands and he gave freely — no request went unanswered.
units.literal: At first Sheji regarded Xianzhi as timid and slow, fearing he could not support himself; by now he had achieved merit, his household wealth was in the tens of thousands, and he could distribute generously — when people made requests, he never refused a word.

units.zh: 其載，入朝，拜開府儀同三司，尋除武威太守、河西節度使，代安思順。
units.en: That year he came to court as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Ceremonial of the Three Dukes, then was made prefect of Wuwei and commissioner of Hexi in place of An Sishun.
units.literal: That year he entered court and was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Ceremonial of the Three Dukes; soon he was made Prefect of Wuwei and Military Commissioner of Hexi, replacing An Sishun.

units.zh: 思順諷群胡割耳捴面請留，監察御史裴周南奏之，制復留思順，以仙芝為右羽林大將軍。
units.en: Sishun stirred the frontier tribes to mutilate themselves in petition to keep him; Censor Pei Zhounan reported it; the emperor retained Sishun and made Xianzhi grand general of the Right Forest of Feathers.
units.literal: Sishun incited the various Hu to cut their ears and smear their faces to beg that he remain; Censor Pei Zhounan memorialized this; an edict kept Sishun in place and made Xianzhi Grand General of the Right Forest of Feathers.

units.zh: 十四載，封密雲郡公。
units.en: In the fourteenth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Miyun.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Miyun commandery.

units.zh: 十一月，安祿山據范陽叛。
units.en: In the eleventh month An Lushan rebelled from Fanyang.
units.literal: In the eleventh month An Lushan seized Fanyang and rebelled.

units.zh: 是日，以京兆牧、榮王琬為討賊元帥，仙芝為副。
units.en: That day Prince Rong Wan, metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, was named commander to suppress the rebels, with Xianzhi as his deputy.
units.literal: That day Prince Rong Wan, Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, was made Commander-in-Chief to Punish the Rebels, with Xianzhi as deputy.

units.zh: 命仙芝領飛騎、彍騎及朔方、河西、隴右應赴京兵馬，並召募關輔五萬人，繼封常清出潼關進討，仍以仙芝兼御史大夫。
units.en: Xianzhi was ordered to take the flying and strong cavalry and the Shuofang, Hexi, and Longyou forces marching to the capital, recruit fifty thousand men from the Guanzhong region, follow Feng Changqing through Tong Pass to attack the rebels, and was made censor-in-chief as well.
units.literal: Xianzhi was ordered to lead the Flying Cavalry, the Strong Cavalry, and the troops of Shuofang, Hexi, and Longyou who were to hurry to the capital, and also to recruit fifty thousand men from Guanfu; he was to follow Feng Changqing out of Tong Pass to advance and attack, and Xianzhi was concurrently made Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 十二月，師發，玄宗禦望春亭慰勞遣之，仍令監門將軍邊令誠監其軍，屯於陜州。
units.en: In the twelfth month the army marched; the emperor saw them off at Wangchun Pavilion and sent Gate-Guard General Bian Lingcheng to supervise the force, which encamped at Shanzhou.
units.literal: In the twelfth month the army set out; Xuanzong attended at Wangchun Pavilion to comfort, reward, and send them off, and again ordered Gate-Guard General Bian Lingcheng to supervise the army, which encamped at Shanzhou.

units.zh: 是月十一日，封常清兵敗於汜水。
units.en: On the eleventh of that month Feng Changqing was defeated at Sishui.
units.literal: On the eleventh day of that month Feng Changqing's army was defeated at Sishui.

units.zh: 十三日，祿山陷東京，常清以餘眾奔陜州，謂仙芝曰：「累日血戰，賊鋒不可當。
units.en: On the thirteenth Lushan took the Eastern Capital; Changqing fled with his survivors to Shanzhou and told Xianzhi, "We have fought for days in blood — the rebel host cannot be stopped.
units.literal: On the thirteenth Lushan took the Eastern Capital; Changqing fled with his remaining troops to Shanzhou and said to Xianzhi: "For days we have fought in blood; the rebels' spearhead cannot be withstood.

units.zh: 且潼關無兵，若狂寇奔突，則京師危矣。
units.en: Tong Pass is undefended; if the rebels break through, the capital is lost.
units.literal: Moreover Tong Pass has no troops; if the mad rebels rush through, the capital will be in peril.

units.zh: 宜棄此守，急保潼關。」
units.en: We must abandon this position and fall back at once to Tong Pass."
units.literal: We should abandon this defense and urgently secure Tong Pass."

units.zh: 常清、仙芝乃率見兵取太原倉錢絹，分給將士，餘皆焚之。
units.en: Changqing and Xianzhi took the cash and silk from the Taiyuan depot, distributed them to the troops, and burned what remained.
units.literal: Changqing and Xianzhi then led the troops at hand to take the money and silk of the Taiyuan granary, distributed them to officers and soldiers, and burned the rest.

units.zh: 俄而賊騎繼至，諸軍惶駭，棄甲而走，無復隊伍。
units.en: Rebel cavalry overtook them; the army panicked, cast off its armor, and fled in disorder.
units.literal: Soon rebel cavalry followed; the armies were terrified and threw off their armor and fled — there were no formations left.

units.zh: 仙芝至關，繕修守具，又令索承光守善和戍。
units.en: At the pass Xianzhi repaired the defenses and posted Suo Chengguang at the Shanhe garrison.
units.literal: When Xianzhi reached the pass he repaired the defensive equipment and also ordered Suo Chengguang to guard the Shanhe garrison.

units.zh: 賊騎至關，已有備矣，不能攻而去，仙芝之力也。
units.en: When the rebels reached the pass they found it ready and withdrew without attacking — thanks to Xianzhi.
units.literal: When rebel cavalry reached the pass, preparations were already in place; they could not attack and withdrew — this was Xianzhi's doing.

units.zh: 封常清，蒲州猗氏人也。
units.en: Feng Changqing was from Yishi in Pu prefecture.
units.literal: Feng Changqing was a man of Yishi in Pu prefecture.

units.zh: 外祖犯罪流安西效力，守胡城南門，頗讀書，每坐常清於城門樓上，教其讀書，多所歷覽。
units.en: His maternal grandfather, banished to Anxi for a crime, guarded the south gate of Hucheng, was well read, and each day sat Changqing on the gate tower to teach him — the boy read widely.
units.literal: His maternal grandfather, having committed a crime, was banished to Anxi to serve; he guarded the south gate of Hucheng, read considerably, and each day seated Changqing on the gate tower to teach him reading — [Changqing] read widely.

units.zh: 外祖死，常清孤貧，年三十餘，屬夫蒙靈察為四鎮節度使，將軍高仙芝為都知兵馬使，頗有材能，每出軍，奏傔從三十餘人，衣服鮮明。
units.en: After his grandfather died Changqing was left poor and alone. Past thirty, Fumeng Lingcha was commissioner of the Four Garrisons and Gao Xianzhi commander — a capable man who marched with thirty-odd brilliantly dressed attendants.
units.literal: When his grandfather died, Changqing was orphaned and poor; past thirty years of age, it happened that Fumeng Lingcha was Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons and General Gao Xianzhi was Commander-in-Chief — quite talented; whenever he went on campaign he memorialized more than thirty personal attendants, their clothes bright and fresh.

units.zh: 常清慨然發憤，投牒請預一傔。
units.en: Changqing, indignant, petitioned to join them as an attendant.
units.literal: Changqing, stirred with indignation, submitted a petition asking to be counted among one attendant.

units.zh: 常清細瘦目類腳短而跛，仙芝見其貌寢，不納。
units.en: Changqing was slight, hollow-eyed, short-legged, and lame; Xianzhi thought him homely and refused him.
units.literal: Changqing was thin and slight, his eyes deep-set, his legs short and lame; Xianzhi saw his appearance was poor and did not accept him.

units.zh: 明日又投牒，仙芝謂曰：「吾奏傔已足，何煩復來！」
units.en: The next day he petitioned again. Xianzhi said, "My attendants are full — why keep coming back?"
units.literal: The next day he submitted another petition; Xianzhi said to him: "My memorial attendants are already sufficient — why trouble to come again!"

units.zh: 常清怒，倨謂仙芝曰：「常清慕公高義，願事鞭轡，所以無媒而前，何見拒之深乎？
units.en: Changqing flared up and said boldly, "I admire your integrity and wish to serve you — that is why I came unintroduced. Why turn me away so harshly?
units.literal: Changqing grew angry and said haughtily to Xianzhi: "Changqing admires your lofty integrity and wishes to serve at whip and bridle; that is why I came forward without a go-between — why reject me so deeply?

units.zh: 公若方圓取人，則士大夫所望；
units.en: If you judge men by their talent and character, that is what gentlemen expect;
units.literal: If you take men by their capacity and integrity, that is what scholars and officials hope for;

units.zh: 若以貌取人，恐失之子羽矣！」
units.en: if you judge by looks alone, you may lose another Ziyu!"
units.literal: if you take men by appearance, I fear you will lose them as with Ziyu!"

units.zh: 仙芝猶未納。
units.en: Xianzhi still refused him.
units.literal: Xianzhi still did not accept him.

units.zh: 常清自爾候仙芝出入，晨夕不離其門，凡數十日，仙芝不得已，補為傔。
units.en: Thereafter Changqing attended Xianzhi's door morning and night for many days until Xianzhi, unable to refuse further, made him an attendant.
units.literal: From then on Changqing waited on Xianzhi's comings and goings, morning and evening never leaving his gate; after several tens of days Xianzhi had no choice and appointed him an attendant.

units.zh: 開元末，會達奚部落背叛，自黑山北向，西趣碎葉，玄宗敕靈察邀擊之。
units.en: Late in Kaiyuan the Daxi tribes rebelled, marching north from Black Mountain toward Suyab; the emperor ordered Lingcha to intercept them.
units.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era the Daxi tribes rebelled, marching north from Black Mountain and turning west toward Suyab; Xuanzong ordered Lingcha to intercept and attack them.

units.zh: 靈察使仙芝以二千騎自副城向北至綾嶺下，遇賊擊之。
units.en: Lingcha sent Xianzhi with two thousand horsemen from Fucheng to Lingling Ridge, where they met and attacked the rebels.
units.literal: Lingcha sent Xianzhi with two thousand cavalry from Fucheng north to below Lingling Ridge, where they met the rebels and attacked.

units.zh: 達奚行遠，人馬皆疲，斬殺略盡。
units.en: The Daxi were exhausted from the long march; nearly all were cut down.
units.literal: The Daxi had marched far; men and horses were all exhausted — they were cut down and killed almost to the last.

units.zh: 常清於幕中潛作捷書，具言次舍井泉，遇賊形勢，克獲謀略，事頗精審。
units.en: In camp Changqing secretly drafted the victory report, detailing every halt, well, encounter, and stratagem with meticulous precision.
units.literal: In the tent Changqing secretly drafted the victory report, fully detailing encampments and wells, the situation on meeting the enemy, and the strategy of capture — the matter was quite precise and thorough.

units.zh: 仙芝所欲言，無不周悉，仙芝大駭異之。
units.en: Everything Xianzhi would have said was there, complete; Xianzhi was astonished.
units.literal: Whatever Xianzhi wished to say was all covered completely; Xianzhi was greatly startled and regarded him as extraordinary.

units.zh: 仙芝軍回，靈察賞勞，仙芝去奴襪帶刀見。
units.en: When the army returned Lingcha held a reward ceremony; Xianzhi doffed his servant's hose, buckled on his sword, and presented himself.
units.literal: When Xianzhi's army returned, Lingcha rewarded and comforted them; Xianzhi removed his slave's socks, belted on his sword, and went to see him.

units.zh: 判官劉眺、獨孤峻等逆問之曰：「前者捷書，誰之所作？
units.en: Judge Liu Tiao and Dugu Jun pressed him: "Who wrote that victory report?
units.literal: Judge Liu Tiao, Dugu Jun, and others pressed him, asking: "That earlier victory report — who wrote it?

units.zh: 副大使幕下何得有如此人」仙芝曰：「即仙芝傔人封常清也。」
units.en: How could your staff hold such a man?" Xianzhi said, "My attendant Feng Changqing."
units.literal: How could the Deputy Commissioner's staff have such a man?" Xianzhi said: "It is my attendant Feng Changqing."

units.zh: 眺等揖仙芝，命常清進坐，與語如舊相識，眾人方異之。
units.en: Tiao and the others bowed to Xianzhi and had Changqing sit with them, talking as with an old friend; the company marveled.
units.literal: Tiao and the others bowed to Xianzhi, ordered Changqing to come forward and sit, and spoke with him as with an old acquaintance — only then did the crowd regard him as extraordinary.

units.zh: 以破達奚功，授疊州地下戍主，便以為判官。
units.en: For defeating the Daxi he was made garrison chief at Diezhou and appointed judge on the spot.
units.literal: For the merit of defeating the Daxi he was appointed garrison chief of the Diezhou underground post and at once made a judge.

units.zh: 累以軍功授鎮將、果毅、折沖。
units.en: Through repeated victories he rose to garrison general, guoyi, and zhechong.
units.literal: Through repeated military merit he was appointed garrison general, guoyi, and zhechong.

units.zh: 天寶六年，從仙芝破小勃律。
units.en: In Tianbao 6 he followed Xianzhi in the conquest of Lesser Bolü.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao he followed Xianzhi in defeating Lesser Bolü.

units.zh: 十二月，仙芝代夫蒙靈察為安西節度使，便奏常清為慶王府錄事參軍，充節度判官，賜紫金魚袋。
units.en: In the twelfth month Xianzhi replaced Lingcha as commissioner of Anxi and had Changqing made recorder on the Prince of Qing's staff, commission judge, and granted a purple-gold fish tally.
units.literal: In the twelfth month Xianzhi replaced Fumeng Lingcha as Military Commissioner of Anxi and at once memorialized Changqing as Recorder of the Prince of Qing's mansion, serving as the commissioner's judge, and granted a purple-gold fish tally.

units.zh: 尋加朝散大夫，專知四鎮倉庫、屯田、甲仗、支度、營田事。
units.en: He was soon made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and put in charge of the Four Garrisons' stores, garrison agriculture, arms, disbursements, and military colonies.
units.literal: Soon he was given the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and put in sole charge of the Four Garrisons' granaries, garrison fields, armor and weapons, disbursements, and military colonies.

units.zh: 仙芝每出征討，常令常清知留後事。
units.en: Whenever Xianzhi campaigned he left Changqing in charge at headquarters.
units.literal: Whenever Xianzhi went on campaign to attack, he always left Changqing in charge of rear affairs.

units.zh: 常清有才學，果決。
units.en: Changqing was learned, capable, and decisive.
units.literal: Changqing had learning and talent and was resolute.

units.zh: 知留後時，仙芝乳母子鄭德詮已為郎將，德銓母在宅內，仙芝視之如兄弟，家事皆令知之，威望動三軍。
units.en: As rear commander, Xianzhi's foster brother Zheng Dequan was already a langjiang; Xianzhi treated Dequan and his mother like family and let them into every household matter — their sway over the army was immense.
units.literal: While in charge of rear affairs, Xianzhi's foster brother Zheng Dequan was already a langjiang; Dequan's mother was in the residence; Xianzhi treated them like brothers and let them know all household affairs — their prestige moved the whole army.

units.zh: 常清出回，諸將皆引前，德詮見常清出其門，素易之，自後走馬突常清而去。
units.en: When Changqing returned, the generals made way; Dequan, who had always despised him, spurred his horse and rode straight through him from behind.
units.literal: When Changqing came out on his return, all the generals drew aside before him; Dequan saw Changqing emerge from his gate, had always looked down on him, and from behind spurred his horse and charged through Changqing to pass.

units.zh: 常清至使院，命左右密引至，厅連節度使宅院，凡經數重門，德詮既過，命隨後閉之。
units.en: Changqing went to headquarters and had his men bring Dequan in secretly through the linked gates of the commissioner's compound; once Dequan had passed, the gates were shut behind him.
units.literal: Changqing went to the commissioner's courtyard, ordered his attendants to lead Dequan in secretly; the hall connected with the commissioner's residence through several gates in succession — once Dequan had passed, he ordered them closed behind him.

units.zh: 德詮至，常清離席謂之曰：「常清起自細微，預中丞兵馬使傔，中丞再不納，郎將豈不知乎？
units.en: When Dequan arrived Changqing rose and said, "I came from nothing and twice asked to serve the Vice Commissioner as attendant — he refused me both times. You know that, do you not?
units.literal: When Dequan arrived, Changqing rose from his seat and said to him: "Changqing rose from humble origins and sought to join the Vice Commissioner's attendants; the Vice Commissioner twice refused me — does the langjiang not know this?

units.zh: 今中丞過聽，以常清為留後使，郎將何得無禮，對中使相淩！」
units.en: Now the Vice Commissioner has made me rear commander — how dare you show such disrespect before a palace envoy!"
units.literal: Now the Vice Commissioner has over-listened and made Changqing rear commander — how can the langjiang be so rude as to bully a palace envoy to his face!"

units.zh: 因叱之曰：「郎將須暫死以肅軍容。」
units.en: He shouted, "You must die for a moment to restore discipline in the ranks."
units.literal: He then shouted at him: "The langjiang must die for a time to restore military discipline."

units.zh: 因令勒回，杖六十，面仆地，曳出。
units.en: He had him brought back, beaten sixty strokes, face down, and dragged out.
units.literal: He then ordered him brought back, flogged sixty strokes, face down on the ground, and dragged out.

units.zh: 仙芝妻及乳母於門外號哭救之，不得，因以其狀上仙芝。
units.en: Xianzhi's wife and foster mother wailed at the gate in vain and reported the affair to Xianzhi.
units.literal: Xianzhi's wife and foster mother wailed at the gate to save him but could not; they therefore reported the matter up to Xianzhi.

units.zh: 仙芝覽之，驚曰：「已死矣！」
units.en: Xianzhi read the report and cried in alarm, "He is dead!"
units.literal: Xianzhi read it and said in alarm: "He is already dead!"

units.zh: 及見常清，遂無一言，常清亦不之謝。
units.en: When he saw Changqing he said nothing; Changqing offered no thanks.
units.literal: When he met Changqing he said not a word; Changqing also did not thank him.

units.zh: 諸大將有罪者，擊殺二人，於是軍中股慄。
units.en: He executed two guilty senior officers, and the whole army trembled.
units.literal: Among the great generals who were guilty, two were struck down and killed; from this the army trembled in awe.

units.zh: 十載，仙芝改西節度使，奏常清為判官。
units.en: In the tenth year Xianzhi became commissioner of the West and had Changqing made his judge.
units.literal: In the tenth year Xianzhi was transferred to be Military Commissioner of the West and memorialized Changqing as judge.

units.zh: 王正見為安西節度，奏常清為四鎮支度營田副使、行軍司馬。
units.en: When Wang Zhengjian became commissioner of Anxi he had Changqing made deputy for disbursements and military colonies and campaigning major.
units.literal: Wang Zhengjian was Military Commissioner of Anxi and memorialized Changqing as Deputy Commissioner for Disbursements and Military Colonies of the Four Garrisons and Campaigning Major.

units.zh: 十一載，正見死，乃以常清為安西副大都護，攝御史中丞，持節充安西四鎮節度、經略、支度、營田副大使，知節度事。
units.en: In the eleventh year, when Zhengjian died, Changqing was made deputy grand protector of Anxi, acting censor-in-chief, and deputy commissioner of the Four Garrisons with full authority over the command.
units.literal: In the eleventh year Zhengjian died; Changqing was then made Deputy Grand Protector-General of Anxi, Acting Censor-in-Chief, bearing the staff as Deputy Commissioner for Military Affairs, Strategy, Disbursements, and Military Colonies of the Four Garrisons of Anxi, and given charge of commission affairs.

units.zh: 十三載入朝，攝御史大夫，仍與一子五品官，賜第一區，亡父母皆贈封爵。
units.en: In the thirteenth year he came to court as acting censor-in-chief, received a fifth-rank post for a son, a mansion, and posthumous titles for his parents.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year he entered court, was made Acting Censor-in-Chief, and one son was given a fifth-rank office; he was granted one first-class residence; his deceased parents were both given posthumous enfeoffments.

units.zh: 俄而北庭都護程千里入為右金吾大將軍，仍令常清權知北庭都護，持節充伊西節度等使。
units.en: Soon Beiting Protector Cheng Qianli was recalled to court; Changqing was left acting protector of Beiting and commissioner of Yixi as well.
units.literal: Soon Beiting Protector Cheng Qianli entered court as Grand General of the Right Golden Crow Guard; Changqing was still ordered to act as Protector of Beiting pro tempore, bearing the staff as Commissioner of Yixi and other posts.

units.zh: 常清性勤儉，每出征或乘驛，私馬不過一兩匹，賞罰嚴明。
units.en: Changqing was frugal and strict: on campaign he used the post relays and kept no more than one or two private horses; his rewards and punishments were exact.
units.literal: Changqing was diligent and frugal by nature; on each campaign he might ride the post relays, keeping no more than one or two private horses; rewards and punishments were strict and clear.

units.zh: 十四載，入朝，十一月，謁玄宗於華清宮。
units.en: In the fourteenth year he came to court and in the eleventh month was received by the emperor at Huaqing Palace.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year he entered court; in the eleventh month he had an audience with Xuanzong at Huaqing Palace.

units.zh: 時祿山已叛，玄宗言兇胡負恩之狀，何方誅討？
units.en: Lushan had already rebelled; the emperor spoke of the rebel's ingratitude and asked how he might be destroyed.
units.literal: At that time Lushan had already rebelled; Xuanzong spoke of how the fierce barbarian had betrayed grace — from what direction should he be punished?

units.zh: 常清奏曰：「祿山領兇徒十萬，徑犯中原，太平斯久，人不知戰。
units.en: Changqing said, "Lushan leads a hundred thousand rebels straight against the heartland; after so long at peace, our people scarcely know war.
units.literal: Changqing memorialized: "Lushan leads a hundred thousand fierce followers and will invade the Central Plains directly; peace has lasted so long that people do not know war.

units.zh: 然事有逆順，勢有奇變，臣請走馬赴東京，開府庫，募驍勇，挑馬箠渡河，計日取逆胡之首懸於闕下。」
units.en: Yet fortune turns, and tactics surprise; let me ride to the Eastern Capital, open the treasuries, raise bold men, ford the river at a gallop, and within days hang the rebel's head at the palace gates."
units.literal: Yet affairs have what is contrary and what is compliant, and situations have strange turns; your servant asks to ride post-horses to the Eastern Capital, open the government stores, recruit the bold and brave, spur horses and cross the river with whips, and within a counted number of days take the rebel barbarian's head and hang it below the palace gates."

units.zh: 玄宗方憂，壯其言。
units.en: The emperor, anxious, took heart from his bold words.
units.literal: Xuanzong was then worried and took strength from his words.

units.zh: 翌日，以常清為范陽節度，俾募兵東討。
units.en: The next day he was made commissioner of Fanyang and ordered east to raise an army.
units.literal: The next day Changqing was made Military Commissioner of Fanyang and ordered to recruit troops for an eastern punitive campaign.

units.zh: 其日，常清乘驛赴東京召募，旬日得兵六萬，皆傭保市井之流。
units.en: That same day he rode post-horses to the Eastern Capital and in ten days raised sixty thousand men — hirelings and street rabble every one.
units.literal: That day Changqing rode the relays to the Eastern Capital to recruit; in ten days he got sixty thousand troops, all hirelings and riffraff of the market streets.

units.zh: 乃斫斷河陽橋，於東京為固守之備。
units.en: He cut the Heyang Bridge and prepared a stubborn defense of the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: He then cut down the Heyang Bridge and made preparations in the Eastern Capital for a stubborn defense.

units.zh: 十二月，祿山渡河，陷陳留，入罌子谷，兇威轉熾，先鋒至葵園。
units.en: In the twelfth month Lushan crossed the river, took Chenliu, entered Yingzigu, and his vanguard reached Kuiyuan as his power swelled.
units.literal: In the twelfth month Lushan crossed the river, took Chenliu, entered Yingzigu; his fierce might grew ever hotter; the vanguard reached Kuiyuan.

units.zh: 常清使驍騎與柘羯逆戰，殺賊數十百人。
units.en: Changqing sent his best horsemen against the Zhejie vanguard and killed several hundred rebels.
units.literal: Changqing sent fierce cavalry to meet the Tujue in battle and killed several tens or hundreds of the enemy.

units.zh: 賊大軍繼至，常清退入上東門，又戰不利，賊鼓噪於四城門入，殺掠人吏。
units.en: The main rebel host followed; Changqing fell back to the Upper East Gate, fought again and lost; the rebels stormed all four gates, killing and plundering throughout the city.
units.literal: The rebel main force followed; Changqing withdrew into the Upper East Gate, fought again without success; the rebels drummed and shouted and entered through the four city gates, killing and plundering officials and clerks.

units.zh: 常清又戰於都亭驛，不勝。
units.en: He fought again at Duting Station and was beaten.
units.literal: Changqing fought again at Duting Post Station and did not prevail.

units.zh: 退守宣仁門，又敗。
units.en: He withdrew to Xuanren Gate and was defeated again.
units.literal: He withdrew to defend Xuaren Gate and was defeated again.

units.zh: 乃從提象門入，倒樹以礙之。
units.en: He retreated through Tixiang Gate and felled trees to block pursuit.
units.literal: He then entered through Tixiang Gate and felled trees to obstruct pursuit.

units.zh: 至谷水，西奔至陜郡，遇高仙芝，具以賊勢告之。
units.en: At the Gu River he fled west to Shan commandery, met Gao Xianzhi, and told him the full strength of the rebel host.
units.literal: Reaching Gu River, he fled west to Shan commandery, met Gao Xianzhi, and fully reported the rebels' strength to him.

units.zh: 恐賊難與爭鋒，仙芝遂退守潼關。
units.en: Fearing the rebels were too strong to meet in the field, Xianzhi withdrew to Tong Pass.
units.literal: Fearing the rebels were hard to contend with in battle, Xianzhi then withdrew to defend Tong Pass.

units.zh: 玄宗聞常清敗，削其官爵，令白衣於仙芝軍效力。
units.en: When the emperor heard of Changqing's defeat he stripped his rank and ordered him to serve in plain clothes under Xianzhi.
units.literal: When Xuanzong heard Changqing had been defeated, he stripped his ranks and titles and ordered him to serve in commoner's dress in Xianzhi's army.

units.zh: 仙芝令常清監巡左右廂諸軍，常清衣皁衣以從事。
units.en: Xianzhi set Changqing to inspect the left and right wings of the army, dressed in plain black.
units.literal: Xianzhi ordered Changqing to supervise and inspect the armies of the left and right wings; Changqing wore black clothes in performing his duties.

units.zh: 監軍邊令誠每事幹之。
units.en: Army supervisor Bian Lingcheng interfered in every decision.
units.literal: Army Supervisor Bian Lingcheng interfered in every matter.

units.zh: 仙芝多不從。
units.en: Xianzhi mostly ignored him.
units.literal: Xianzhi mostly did not follow him.

units.zh: 令誠入奏事，具言仙芝、常清逗撓奔敗之狀。
units.en: Lingcheng reported to court that Xianzhi and Changqing had dallied, fled, and been defeated.
units.literal: Lingcheng entered to report affairs and fully described how Xianzhi and Changqing had dallied, hesitated, fled, and been defeated.

units.zh: 玄宗怒，遣令誠賫敕至軍並誅之。
units.en: The emperor in anger sent Lingcheng with an edict to execute them both.
units.literal: Xuanzong was angry and sent Lingcheng bearing an edict to the army to execute them both.

units.zh: 令誠至潼關，引常清於驛南西街，宣敕示之。
units.en: At Tong Pass Lingcheng led Changqing to the lane south of the post station and read the edict of execution.
units.literal: Lingcheng reached Tong Pass, led Changqing to the west street south of the post station, and proclaimed the edict to show him.

units.zh: 常清曰：「常清所以不死者，不忍汙國家旌麾，受戮賊手，討逆無效，死乃甘心。」
units.en: Changqing said, "I have lived only so as not to die under rebel blades and defile the imperial banners; though I failed against the traitors, I welcome death."
units.literal: Changqing said: "The reason Changqing has not died is that I could not bear to defile the state's banners and standards by being executed at the rebels' hands; though the campaign against the traitors failed, death is what I accept willingly."

units.zh: 初，常清兵敗入關，欲馳赴闕庭，至渭南，有敕令卻赴潼關，自草表待罪。
units.en: After his defeat he had meant to ride to court; at Weinan an edict sent him back to Tong Pass, and he drafted a memorial accepting blame.
units.literal: Earlier, when Changqing's army was defeated and he entered the pass, he wished to ride post-horses to the palace court; reaching Weinan, there was an edict ordering him back to Tong Pass; he himself drafted a memorial awaiting punishment.

units.zh: 是日臨刑，托令誠上之。
units.en: On the day of his execution he gave it to Lingcheng to present.
units.literal: On the day of execution he entrusted it to Lingcheng to submit.

units.zh: 其表曰：
units.en: The memorial read:
units.literal: The memorial read:

units.zh: 中使駱奉仙至，奉宣口敕，恕臣萬死之罪，收臣一朝之效，令臣卻赴陜州，隨高仙芝行營，。
units.en: The palace envoy Luo Fengxian came with an oral edict forgiving my capital crime, accepting my day's service, and ordering me back to Shanzhou under Gao Xianzhi's command.
units.literal: The palace envoy Luo Fengxian arrived and proclaimed an oral edict forgiving your servant's crime deserving ten thousand deaths, accepting your servant's effort of a morning, and ordering your servant to return to Shanzhou to follow Gao Xianzhi's mobile camp.

units.zh: 負斧縲囚，忽焉解縛，敗軍之將，更許增修。
units.en: A condemned prisoner suddenly unbound; a defeated general allowed to redeem himself.
units.literal: Bearing the axe, bound as a prisoner, suddenly the bonds were loosed; a defeated general was again permitted to make amends.

units.zh: 臣常清誠歡誠喜，頓首頓首。
units.en: Your servant Changqing bows in true joy and gratitude.
units.literal: Your servant Changqing is truly joyful, truly glad — bowing head, bowing head.

units.zh: 臣自城陷已來，前後三度遣使奉表，具述赤心，竟不蒙引對。
units.en: Since the city fell I have thrice sent memorials declaring my loyalty, yet never been granted audience.
units.literal: Since the city fell your servant has three times sent envoys with memorials, fully stating my loyal heart, yet I have not been granted an audience.

units.zh: 臣之此來，非求茍活，實欲陳社稷之計，破虎狼之謀。
units.en: I did not come to cling to life but to lay plans for the realm and break the rebels' designs.
units.literal: Your servant's coming here is not to seek a shameful survival but truly to present plans for the altars of state and break the schemes of tiger and wolf.

units.zh: 冀拜首闕庭，吐心陛下，論逆胡之兵勢，陳討捍之別謀。
units.en: I hoped to bow at the palace gates, speak my heart to Your Majesty, describe the rebel armies, and offer other plans for their defeat.
units.literal: I hoped to bow my head at the palace gates, pour out my heart to Your Majesty, discuss the rebel barbarian's military strength, and set forth separate plans for attack and defense.

units.zh: 酬萬死之恩，以報一生之寵。
units.en: To repay the grace that spared me and the favor of a lifetime.
units.literal: To repay grace forgiving ten thousand deaths and requite a lifetime's favor.

units.zh: 豈料長安日遠，謁見無由；
units.en: Who could know that Chang'an would grow ever farther and audience be denied;
units.literal: Who could have expected Chang'an growing daily more distant, with no means to have an audience;

units.zh: 函谷關遙，陳情不暇！
units.en: Hangu Pass so remote that I had no time to speak my heart!
units.literal: Hangu Pass far away — no leisure to state my feelings!

units.zh: 臣讀《春秋》，見狼瞫稱未獲死所，臣今獲矣。
units.en: I read in the Spring and Autumn that Lang Shen said he had not yet found his place to die — I have found mine.
units.literal: Your servant read the Spring and Autumn Annals and saw Langchen say he had not yet found where to die — your servant has found it now.

units.zh: 昨者與羯胡接戰，自今月七日交兵，至於十三日不已。
units.en: We fought the Jie rebels from the seventh of this month until the thirteenth without pause.
units.literal: Yesterday we joined battle with the Jie barbarians; from the seventh of this month we fought until the thirteenth without cease.

units.zh: 臣所將之兵，皆是烏合之徒，素未訓習。
units.en: The men I led were a rabble, never drilled.
units.literal: The troops your servant led were all a mob thrown together, never trained in discipline.

units.zh: 率周南市人之眾，當漁陽突騎之師，尚猶殺敵塞路，血流滿野。
units.en: Leading market rabble against Fanyang's shock cavalry, we still killed until the roads were choked and the fields ran with blood.
units.literal: Leading the crowd of Zhounan market folk against the Fanyang shock-cavalry host, we still killed the enemy until the road was blocked and blood flowed over the fields.

units.zh: 臣欲挺身刃下，死節軍前，恐長逆胡之威，以挫王師之勢。
units.en: I wished to die sword in hand before the ranks, but feared that would only swell the rebels' pride and break our army's spirit.
units.literal: Your servant wished to throw himself under the blades and die in honor before the army, but feared this would lengthen the rebel barbarian's prestige and blunt the imperial army's momentum.

units.zh: 是以馳禦就日，將命歸天。
units.en: So I rode post-horses toward the capital to lay my life before the throne.
units.literal: Therefore I rode post-horses to approach the sun and offer my life back to Heaven.

units.zh: 一期陛下斬臣於都市之下，以誡諸將；
units.en: First, that Your Majesty execute me in the capital to warn the generals;
units.literal: First, that Your Majesty would behead your servant below the market to warn the generals;

units.zh: 二期陛下問臣以逆賊之勢，將誡諸軍；
units.en: second, that Your Majesty question me on the rebels' strength to warn the armies;
units.literal: second, that Your Majesty would question your servant on the rebel traitors' strength to warn the armies;

units.zh: 三期陛下知臣非惜死之徒，許臣竭露。
units.en: third, that Your Majesty know I am no coward and let me speak all I know.
units.literal: third, that Your Majesty would know your servant is not one who clings to life and would permit your servant to pour out everything.

units.zh: 臣今將死抗表，陛下或以臣失律之後，誑妄為辭；
units.en: Facing death I submit this memorial; Your Majesty may think that after my defeat these are the lies of a desperate man;
units.literal: Your servant now, facing death, submits this defiant memorial; Your Majesty may think that after your servant violated discipline these are deceitful, reckless words;

units.zh: 陛下或以臣欲盡所忠，肝膽見察。
units.en: or Your Majesty may see that I speak with all my heart laid bare.
units.literal: or Your Majesty may think your servant wishes to exhaust all loyalty and will perceive my liver and gall laid bare.

units.zh: 臣死之後，望陛下不輕此賊，無忘臣言，則冀社稷復安，逆胡敗覆，臣之所願畢矣。
units.en: After I die, may Your Majesty not underestimate this enemy or forget my words — then the realm may be restored and the rebels destroyed, and my life's wish fulfilled.
units.literal: After your servant dies, I hope Your Majesty will not take this enemy lightly or forget your servant's words — then I may hope the altars of state are restored to peace and the rebel barbarian overthrown; your servant's wishes will be complete.

units.zh: 仰天飲鴆，向日封章，即為屍諫之臣，死作聖朝之鬼。
units.en: I drink poison looking up to Heaven and seal this memorial facing the sun — a corpse that remonstrates, a ghost of the holy court.
units.literal: Looking up to Heaven I drink poison; facing the sun I seal this memorial — I become a minister who remonstrates with his corpse and die a ghost of the holy dynasty.

units.zh: 若使歿而有知，必結草軍前。
units.en: If the dead have knowledge, I shall tie grass before the imperial host.
units.literal: If after death there is awareness, I shall surely tie grass before the army.

units.zh: 回風陣上，引王師之旗鼓，平寇賊之戈鋋。
units.en: On the field of battle I shall guide the imperial banners and level the rebels' weapons.
units.literal: On the wind-turning battle line I shall lead the imperial army's banners and drums and level the bandits' and rebels' spears and blades.

units.zh: 生死酬恩，不任感激，臣常清無任永辭聖代悲戀之至。
units.en: Living or dead I repay Your Majesty's grace, overcome with gratitude — your servant Changqing bids eternal farewell with deepest sorrow.
units.literal: Living or dead I repay grace — overcome with gratitude; your servant Changqing, overcome, forever bids farewell to the holy age with utmost sorrow and longing.

units.zh: 常清既刑，陳其屍於蘧蒢上。
units.en: After Changqing was executed his body was laid on a rush mat.
units.literal: After Changqing was executed, his corpse was displayed on a rush mat.

units.zh: 仙芝歸至厅，令誠索陌刀手百餘人隨而從之，曰：「大夫亦有恩命。」
units.en: Xianzhi returned to headquarters; Lingcheng summoned more than a hundred men with mo dao and followed him, saying, "The Grand Master has an edict too."
units.literal: Xianzhi returned to the hall; Lingcheng sought more than a hundred men with mo dao and followed him, saying: "The Grand Master also has an edict of grace."

units.zh: 仙芝遽下，遂至常清所刑處。
units.en: Xianzhi hurried down to where Changqing had been executed.
units.literal: Xianzhi hurried down and went at once to where Changqing had been executed.

units.zh: 仙芝曰：「我退，罪也，死不辭；
units.en: Xianzhi said, "My retreat was a crime and I do not refuse death;
units.literal: Xianzhi said: "My retreat was a crime; I do not refuse death;

units.zh: 然以我為減截兵糧及賜物等，則誣我也。」
units.en: but to charge me with embezzling rations and imperial gifts is slander."
units.literal: but to charge me with cutting down rations and imperial gifts and the like — that is slander against me."

units.zh: 謂令誠曰：「上是天，下是地，兵士皆在，足下豈不知乎！」
units.en: He said to Lingcheng, "Heaven is above, earth below, and the soldiers are all here — you know the truth!"
units.literal: He said to Lingcheng: "Above is Heaven, below is Earth, the soldiers are all here — do you not know, sir!"

units.zh: 其召募兵排列在外，素愛仙芝，仙芝呼謂之曰：「我於京中召兒郎輩，雖得少許物，裝束亦未能足，方與君輩破賊，然後取高官重賞。
units.en: The recruited troops stood outside; they had always loved Xianzhi. He called to them, "When I raised you in the capital we got a little gear but not enough; we were about to break the rebels and win rank and reward together.
units.literal: The recruited troops were lined up outside; they had always loved Xianzhi; Xianzhi called to them: "When I recruited you fellows in the capital, though we got a few things, equipment was still not sufficient; we were just about to break the rebels with you and then take high office and heavy rewards.

units.zh: 不謂賊勢憑陵，引軍至此，亦欲固守潼關故也。
units.en: I did not expect the rebels to press so hard; we came here to hold Tong Pass.
units.literal: I did not expect the rebels' power to press upon us and lead the army here — it was also because we wished to hold Tong Pass firmly.

units.zh: 我若實有此，君輩即言實；
units.en: If I truly did these things, say so;
units.literal: If I truly did this, you fellows speak the truth;

units.zh: 我若實無之，君輩當言枉。」
units.en: if I did not, say I am wronged."
units.literal: if I truly did not, you fellows must say it is wrongful."

units.zh: 兵齊呼曰：「枉」，其聲殷地。
units.en: The soldiers roared "Wronged!" until the ground shook.
units.literal: The soldiers all shouted "Wrongful!" — the sound shook the ground.

units.zh: 仙芝又目常清之屍，謂之曰：「封二，子從微至著，我則引拔子為我判官，俄又代我為節度使，今日又與子同死於此，豈命也夫！」
units.en: Xianzhi looked at Changqing's corpse and said, "Feng the Second, you rose from nothing; I made you my judge, then you replaced me as commissioner, and today we die together — is this fate?"
units.literal: Xianzhi again looked at Changqing's corpse and said to it: "Feng the Second, you rose from humble to prominence; I drew you up to be my judge, soon you replaced me as military commissioner, and today you die here with me — is it fate!"

units.zh: 遂斬之。
units.en: Then he was beheaded.
units.literal: He was then beheaded.

units.zh: 哥舒翰，突騎施首領哥舒部落之裔也。
units.en: Ge Shuhan was descended from the Geshu tribe of the Turgesh.
units.literal: Ge Shuhan was a descendant of the Geshu tribe, chieftains of the Turgesh.

units.zh: 蕃人多以部落稱姓，因以為氏。
units.en: Many frontier peoples took their clan name from their tribe, and so the name Geshu became their surname.
units.literal: Many barbarians take their surname from the tribal name, and thus it became their clan name.

units.zh: 祖沮，左清道率。
units.en: His grandfather Ju was Left Commander of the Clear Way.
units.literal: His grandfather Ju was Left Commander of the Clear Way.

units.zh: 父道元，安西副都護，世居安西。
units.en: His father Daoyuan was deputy protector of Anxi; the family had lived in the west for generations.
units.literal: His father Daoyuan was Deputy Protector-General of Anxi; the family had long resided in Anxi.

units.zh: 翰家富於財，倜儻任俠，好然諾，縱蒲酒。
units.en: The Hans were wealthy; he was bold and chivalrous, kept his word, and gambled and drank freely.
units.literal: The Han family was rich in wealth; he was bold and chivalrous, fond of keeping promises, and indulged in gambling and wine.

units.zh: 年四十，遭父喪，三年客居京師，為長安尉不禮，慨然發憤折節，仗劍之河西。
units.en: At forty, after his father's death, he spent three years in the capital as a guest; the Chang'an commandant slighted him, and in indignation he reformed himself, took up his sword, and went west to Hexi.
units.literal: At forty he suffered his father's death; for three years he lodged as a guest in the capital; the Chang'an commandant treated him without courtesy; stirred with indignation he reformed himself, took sword in hand, and went to Hexi.

units.zh: 初事節度使王倕，倕攻新城，使翰經略，三軍無不震懾。
units.en: He first served Commissioner Wang Chui; when Chui attacked Xincheng he put Han in charge of strategy, and the whole army stood in awe of him.
units.literal: At first he served Military Commissioner Wang Yi; when Yi attacked Xincheng he had Han conduct strategy — the whole army was awed without exception.

units.zh: 後節度使王忠嗣補為衙將。
units.en: Later Commissioner Wang Zhongsi made him a yamen general.
units.literal: Later Military Commissioner Wang Zhongsi appointed him a yamen general.

units.zh: 翰好讀《左氏春秋傳》及《漢書》，疏財重氣，士多歸之。
units.en: He loved the Zuo Commentary and the Book of Han, gave freely, and valued loyalty; men of talent flocked to him.
units.literal: Han loved to read the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Book of Han; he gave freely and valued honor — many gentlemen attached to him.

units.zh: 忠嗣以為大鬥軍副使，嘗使翰討吐蕃於新城，有同列為副者，見翰禮倨，不為用，翰怒，撾殺之，軍中股怵。
units.en: Zhongsi made him deputy of the Great Battle Army and once sent him against Tibet at Xincheng; a fellow deputy refused his orders because Han was arrogant — Han beat him to death, and the army trembled.
units.literal: Zhongsi made him deputy commander of the Great Battle Army; he once sent Han to attack Tibet at Xincheng; a colleague serving as deputy saw Han's courtesy was arrogant and would not obey — Han in anger beat him to death, and the army trembled in fear.

units.zh: 遷左衛郎將。
units.en: He was promoted to langjiang of the Left Guard.
units.literal: He was transferred to Left Guard Langjiang.

units.zh: 後吐蕃寇邊，翰拒之於苦拔海，其眾三行，從山差池而下，翰持半段槍當其鋒擊之，三行皆敗，無不摧靡，由是知名。
units.en: When Tibet raided the border he met them at Kubo Sea; their army descended the mountains in three columns; Han with a short spear charged the van and shattered all three — from that he won fame.
units.literal: Later when Tibet raided the border, Han resisted them at Kubo Sea; their host came in three lines descending staggered from the mountains; Han with a half-length spear met their spearhead and struck — all three lines were defeated, none not shattered; from this he became famous.

units.zh: 天寶六載，擢授右武衛員外將軍，充隴西節度副使、都知關西兵馬使、河源軍使。
units.en: In Tianbao 6 he was made acting general of the Right Martial Guard, deputy commissioner of Longxi, commander of Guanxi forces, and commander of the Heyuan army.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao he was promoted to Acting General of the Right Martial Guard, serving as Deputy Military Commissioner of Longxi, Commander-in-Chief of Guanxi forces, and commander of Heyuan Army.

units.zh: 先是，吐蕃每至麥熟時，即率部眾至積石軍獲取之，共呼為「吐蕃麥莊」，前後無敢拒之者。
units.en: Each harvest season Tibet had raided Jishi to seize the grain — the "Tibetan wheat estate" — and no one had dared resist.
units.literal: Earlier, whenever grain ripened Tibet would lead its tribes to Jishi Army to seize the harvest — all called it the "Tibetan wheat estate" — and none had dared resist before.

units.zh: 至是，翰使王難得、楊景暉等潛引兵至積石軍，設伏以待之。
units.en: Han sent Wang Nande and Yang Jinghui to Jishi with a hidden force to ambush them.
units.literal: At this point Han sent Wang Nande, Yang Jinghui, and others to lead troops secretly to Jishi Army and set an ambush to await them.

units.zh: 吐蕃以五千騎至，翰於城中率驍勇馳擊，殺之略盡，餘或挺走，伏兵邀擊，匹馬不還。
units.en: Five thousand Tibetan horsemen came; Han led a charge from the city and killed nearly all; the survivors fled into the ambush — not one horse returned.
units.literal: Tibet came with five thousand cavalry; Han from within the city led fierce warriors in a charge, killing nearly all; the rest fled or bolted — the ambush intercepted them — not a single horse returned.

units.zh: 翰有家奴曰左軍，年十五六，亦有膂力。
units.en: His slave Zuojun, fifteen or sixteen, was strong as well.
units.literal: Han had a household slave named Zuojun, fifteen or sixteen years old, who also had strength in his arms.

units.zh: 翰善使槍，追賊及之，以槍搭其肩而喝之，賊驚顧，翰從而刺其喉，皆剔高三五尺而墮，無不死者。
units.en: Han was a master of the spear; overtaking a foe he laid the spear on his shoulder and shouted; when the man turned Han stabbed his throat and hurled him several feet — none survived.
units.literal: Han was skilled with the spear; pursuing the enemy he caught up, laid the spear on the man's shoulder and shouted — the enemy turned in alarm and Han then stabbed his throat; all were thrown three or five feet high and fell — none did not die.

units.zh: 左車輒下馬斬首，率以為常。
units.en: Zuoche would dismount and take heads — his usual practice.
units.literal: Zuoche would dismount and cut off heads — this became his habit.

units.zh: 其冬，玄宗在華清宮，王忠嗣被劾。
units.en: That winter, while the emperor was at Huaqing Palace, Wang Zhongsi was impeached.
units.literal: That winter Xuanzong was at Huaqing Palace; Wang Zhongsi was impeached.

units.zh: 敕召翰至，與語悅之，遂以為鴻臚卿，兼西平郡太守，攝御史中丞，代忠嗣為隴右節度支度營田副大使，知節度事。
units.en: Han was summoned to court; the emperor was pleased with him and made him Chamberlain for Court Ceremonials (Honglu qing), prefect of Xiping, acting Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief, and acting Longyou commissioner for disbursements and military colonies in Zhongsi's place, in charge of commission affairs.
units.literal: An edict summoned Han; the emperor spoke with him and was pleased, then made him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently Prefect of Xiping commandery, Acting Censor-in-Chief, replacing Zhongsi as Deputy Commissioner for Disbursements and Military Colonies of Longyou and giving him charge of commission affairs.

units.zh: 仍極言救忠嗣，上起入禁中，翰叩頭隨之而前，言詞慷慨，聲淚俱下，帝感而寬之，貶忠嗣為漢陽太守，朝廷義而壯之。
units.en: He pleaded passionately for Zhongsi; the emperor withdrew to the inner palace and Han followed, kowtowing, speaking with passion through tears; the emperor was moved and demoted Zhongsi to prefect of Hanyang — the court admired his loyalty.
units.literal: He also spoke urgently to save Zhongsi; the emperor rose and entered the inner palace — Han kowtowed and followed forward, his words impassioned, voice and tears together; the emperor was moved and showed leniency, demoting Zhongsi to Prefect of Hanyang; the court praised Han's righteousness and admired his courage.

units.zh: 明年，築神威軍於青海上，吐蕃至，攻破之；
units.en: The next year he built Shenwei garrison on the Qinghai; Tibet came and destroyed it;
units.literal: The next year he built the Shenwei Army on the Qinghai; Tibet came and stormed it;

units.zh: 又築城於青海中龍駒島，有白龍見，遂名為應龍城，吐蕃屏跡不敢近青海。
units.en: then built a city on Dragon Colt Island in the lake; a white dragon was seen, and it was named Responding Dragon City — Tibet dared not approach the Qinghai again.
units.literal: he also built a city on Dragon Colt Island in the midst of Qinghai; a white dragon appeared, so it was named Responding Dragon City — Tibet withdrew and dared not approach Qinghai.

units.zh: 吐蕃保石堡城，路遠而險，久不拔。
units.en: Tibet held Shibao Fortress, distant and perilous — for years it could not be taken.
units.literal: Tibet held Shibao Fortress; the road was distant and perilous — for long it could not be taken.

units.zh: 八載，以朔方、河東群牧十萬眾委翰總統攻石堡城。
units.en: In the eighth year a hundred thousand men from the Shuofang and Hedong horse herds were placed under Han to take Shibao.
units.literal: In the eighth year a hundred thousand men of the Shuofang and Hedong horse herds were entrusted to Han to command the attack on Shibao Fortress.

units.zh: 翰使麾下將高秀巖、張守瑜進攻，不旬日而拔之。
units.en: Han sent Gao Xiuyan and Zhang Shouyu to attack; within ten days the fortress fell.
units.literal: Han sent his generals Gao Xiuyan and Zhang Shouyu to attack; in less than ten days it was taken.

units.zh: 上錄其功，拜特進、鴻臚員外卿，與一子五品官，賜物千匹、莊宅各一所，加攝御史大夫。
units.en: The emperor rewarded him with Special Advancement, acting supernumerary Chamberlain for Court Ceremonials, a fifth-rank post for a son, a thousand bolts of goods, a manor and a residence, and acting Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: The emperor recorded his merit, appointed him Special Advancement and Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, granted a fifth-rank office to one son, bestowed a thousand bolts of goods and one manor each, and added Acting Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 十一載，加開府儀同三司。
units.en: In the eleventh year he was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Ceremonial of the Three Dukes.
units.literal: In the eleventh year he was given Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Ceremonial of the Three Dukes.

units.zh: 翰素與祿山、思順不協，上每和解之為兄弟。
units.en: Han had long been at odds with Lushan and Sishun; the emperor often reconciled them as brothers.
units.literal: Han had long been at odds with Lushan and Sishun; the emperor often reconciled them as brothers.

units.zh: 其冬，祿山、思順、翰並來朝，上使內侍高力士及中貴人於京城東駙馬崔惠童池亭宴會。
units.en: That winter all three came to court; the emperor had Gao Lishi and other eunuchs entertain them at the pool pavilion of Cui Huitong east of the capital.
units.literal: That winter Lushan, Sishun, and Han all came to court; the emperor had the palace attendant Gao Lishi and middle-rank eunuchs hold a banquet at the pool pavilion of the imperial son-in-law Cui Huitong east of the capital.

units.zh: 翰母尉遲氏，於闐之族也。
units.en: Han's mother was of the Yuchi clan, from Khotan.
units.literal: Han's mother was of the Yuchi clan, a Khotanese family.

units.zh: 祿山以思順惡翰，嘗銜之，至是忽謂翰曰：「我父是胡，母是突厥；
units.en: Lushan, who disliked Han because Sishun did, suddenly said, "My father was Hu and my mother Turkic;
units.literal: Lushan, because Sishun disliked Han, had long harbored resentment; now he suddenly said to Han: "My father was a Hu, my mother was Turkic;

units.zh: 公父是突厥，母是胡。
units.en: your father was Turkic and your mother Hu.
units.literal: your father was Turkic, your mother was Hu.

units.zh: 與公族類同，何不相親乎？」
units.en: We are kin — why should we not be friends?"
units.literal: We are of the same kind of clan — why not be close?"

units.zh: 翰應之曰：「古人雲，野狐向窟嗥，不祥，以其忘本也。
units.en: Han replied, "The ancients said a wild fox howling at its den is ill omened — it has forgotten its roots.
units.literal: Han replied: "The ancients said that when a wild fox howls toward its den it is inauspicious, because it has forgotten its roots.

units.zh: 敢不盡心焉！」
units.en: How could I not give you my whole heart!"
units.literal: How dare I not give my whole heart!"

units.zh: 祿山以為譏其胡也，大怒，罵翰曰：「突厥敢如此耶！」
units.en: Lushan thought this mocked his foreign birth and raged, cursing, "How dare a Turk speak so!"
units.literal: Lushan thought this mocked his Hu origin and grew greatly angry, cursing Han: "How dare a Turk act thus!"

units.zh: 翰欲應之，高力士目翰，翰遂止。
units.en: Han started to reply; Gao Lishi caught his eye and Han held his tongue.
units.literal: Han wished to answer; Gao Lishi signaled Han with his eyes, and Han stopped.

units.zh: 十二載，進封涼國公，食實封三百戶，加河西節度使，尋封西平郡王。
units.en: In the twelfth year he was made Duke of Liang with three hundred households, commissioner of Hexi, and soon Prince of Xiping.
units.literal: In the twelfth year he was advanced to Duke of Liang state with three hundred households of substantive enfeoffment, made Military Commissioner of Hexi, and soon enfeoffed as Prince of Xiping commandery.

units.zh: 時楊國忠有隙於祿山，頻奏其反狀，故厚賞翰以親結之。
units.en: Yang Guozhong was at odds with Lushan and repeatedly reported his rebellious intentions; he richly rewarded Han to win his loyalty.
units.literal: At that time Yang Guozhong was at odds with Lushan and repeatedly memorialized his rebellious signs; therefore he richly rewarded Han to bind him in friendship.

units.zh: 十三載，拜太子太保，更加實封三百戶，又兼御史大夫。
units.en: In the thirteenth year he was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, given another three hundred households, and made censor-in-chief as well.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, given another three hundred households of substantive enfeoffment, and also made Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 翰好飲酒，頗恣聲色。
units.en: Han drank heavily and indulged in pleasure.
units.literal: Han loved drinking and indulged considerably in music and women.

units.zh: 至土門軍，入浴室，遘風疾，絕倒良久乃蘇。
units.en: At Tumen garrison he entered the bathhouse, suffered a stroke, and collapsed for a long while before reviving.
units.literal: Reaching Tumen Army, he entered the bathhouse, suffered a wind ailment, collapsed unconscious for a long while before reviving.

units.zh: 因入京，廢疾於家。
units.en: He returned to the capital and was disabled by illness at home.
units.literal: He therefore entered the capital and was disabled by illness at home.

units.zh: 及安祿山反，上以封常清、高仙芝喪敗，召翰入，拜為皇太子先鋒兵馬元帥，以田良丘為御史中丞，充行軍司馬，以王思禮、鉗耳大福、李承光、蘇法鼎、管崇嗣及蕃將火拔歸仁、李武定、渾萼、契苾寧等為裨將，河隴、朔方兵及蕃兵與高仙芝舊卒共二十萬，拒賊於潼關。
units.en: When An Lushan rebelled, because Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi had been defeated, the emperor summoned Han and appointed him Vanguard Commander of the Heir Apparent's Army; Tian Liangqiu was made Vice Censor-in-Chief and Campaigning Major; Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Su Fading, Guan Chongsi, and the barbarian generals Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun E, Qibi Ning, and others were made deputy generals — Hexi, Longyou, and Shuofang troops and barbarian soldiers together with Gao Xianzhi's old troops, two hundred thousand in all, to resist the rebels at Tong Pass.
units.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, because Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi had been defeated and lost, the emperor summoned Han and appointed him Vanguard Commander of the Heir Apparent's Army; Tian Liangqiu was made Censor-in-Chief and Campaigning Major; Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Su Fading, Guan Chongsi, and barbarian generals Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun E, Qibi Ning, and others were made deputy generals — Hexi, Longyou, Shuofang troops and barbarian soldiers together with Gao Xianzhi's old troops, two hundred thousand in all, to resist the rebels at Tong Pass.

units.zh: 上御勤政樓勞遣之，百僚出餞於郊。
units.en: The emperor saw them off from the Hall of Diligent Government; the officials feasted them outside the walls.
units.literal: The emperor attended at the Hall of Diligent Government to comfort and send them off; the hundred officials went out to feast them at the suburbs.

units.zh: 十五載，加翰尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事。
units.en: In the fifteenth year he was made Left Vice Director and Associate Grand Councilor.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year Han was given Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and made Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

units.zh: 翰至潼關，或勸翰曰：「祿山阻兵，以誅楊國忠為名，公若留兵三萬守關，悉以精銳回誅國忠，此漢挫七國之計也，公以為何如？」
units.en: At Tong Pass someone advised him, "Lushan marches under the banner of punishing Yang Guozhong — leave thirty thousand to hold the pass and march your best troops back to kill Guozhong, as the Han did against the Seven States — what say you?"
units.literal: When Han reached Tong Pass, someone advised him: "Lushan blocks the army and takes punishing Yang Guozhong as his pretext — if you leave thirty thousand to guard the pass and bring all your elite back to execute Guozhong, this is the Han plan for breaking the Seven States — what do you think?"

units.zh: 翰心許之，未發。
units.en: Han agreed in his heart but did not act.
units.literal: Han agreed in his heart but did not set out.

units.zh: 有客泄其謀於國忠，國忠大懼，及奏曰：「兵法『安不忘危』，今潼關兵眾雖盛，而無後殿，萬一不利，京師得無恐乎！
units.en: Someone leaked the plan to Guozhong, who in terror memorialized, "In peace forget not danger — Tong Pass is strong but has no reserve; if things go wrong, will not the capital tremble?
units.literal: A guest leaked the plan to Guozhong; Guozhong was greatly afraid and memorialized: "In military law, 'In peace do not forget danger' — now Tong Pass has a great host but no rear guard; if by chance things go ill, will not the capital be in fear!

units.zh: 請選監牧小兒三千人訓練於苑中。」
units.en: He asked to train three thousand boys from the horse herds in the imperial park."
units.literal: He asked to select three thousand boys of the horse herds to train in the imperial park."

units.zh: 詔從之，遂遣劍南軍將李福、劉光庭分統焉。
units.en: The emperor agreed and sent Jiannan generals Li Fu and Liu Guangting to command them.
units.literal: An edict approved this; Li Fu and Liu Guangting of the Jiannan army were then sent to command them separately.

units.zh: 又奏召募一萬人，屯於灞上，令其腹心杜乾運將之。
units.en: He also recruited ten thousand men at Bashang under his confidant Du Qianyun.
units.literal: He also memorialized to recruit ten thousand men to encamp at Bashang, putting his confidant Du Qianyun in command.

units.zh: 翰慮為所圖，乃上表請乾運兵隸於潼關，遂召乾運赴潼關計事，因斬之。
units.en: Han feared a plot against him, asked that Qianyun's troops be attached to Tong Pass, summoned Qianyun there on pretense of consultation, and executed him.
units.literal: Han feared he was being plotted against; he therefore memorialized asking that Qianyun's troops be placed under Tong Pass, then summoned Qianyun to Tong Pass to discuss affairs and beheaded him.

units.zh: 自是，翰心不自安。
units.en: From then on Han was uneasy.
units.literal: From this Han's heart was ill at ease.

units.zh: 又素有風疾，至是頗甚，軍中之務，不復躬親，委政於行軍司馬田良丘。
units.en: His old stroke had worsened; he no longer managed army affairs himself but left them to Tian Liangqiu.
units.literal: He had long had a wind ailment; by now it was quite severe — military affairs he no longer handled in person but entrusted government to Campaigning Major Tian Liangqiu.

units.zh: 良丘復不敢專斷，教令不一，頗無部伍。
units.en: Liangqiu dared not decide alone; orders conflicted and discipline collapsed.
units.literal: Liangqiu in turn did not dare decide alone; orders and teachings were not unified — discipline was quite lacking.

units.zh: 其將王思禮、李承光又爭長不葉，人無鬥志。
units.en: Generals Wang Sili and Li Chengguang vied for command and would not cooperate — the men lost heart.
units.literal: His generals Wang Sili and Li Chengguang also vied for precedence and would not cooperate — men had no fighting spirit.

units.zh: 先是，翰數奏祿山雖竊河朔，而不得人心，請持重以弊之，彼自離心，因而翦滅之，可不傷兵擒茲寇矣。
units.en: Han had repeatedly urged that though Lushan had seized Hebei he lacked popular support — hold firm and wear them down, let them split of themselves, and destroy this bandit without heavy losses.
