units.literal: Earlier Han had repeatedly memorialized that though Lushan had seized Hebei and Shuofang he had not won men's hearts; he asked to hold firm and wear them down — they would split of themselves, and thus he could cut them off and capture this bandit without harming the troops.

units.zh: 賊將崔乾祐於陜郡潛鋒蓄銳，而覘者奏雲「賊殊無備」，上然之，命悉眾速討之。
units.en: Rebel general Cui Qianyu was secretly massing at Shan, but scouts reported "the rebels were unprepared"; the emperor believed it and ordered a full assault at once.
units.literal: The rebel general Cui Qianyu at Shan commandery secretly sharpened his edge and stored his strength, but scouts reported "the rebels are quite unprepared"; the emperor agreed and ordered the whole force to attack quickly.

units.zh: 翰奏曰：「賊既始為AT逆，祿山久習用兵，必不肯無備，是陰計也。
units.en: Han memorialized, "The rebels have risen in treason; Lushan is a veteran commander — he will not be unprepared; this is a trap.
units.literal: Han memorialized: "Since the rebels have begun treason, Lushan has long practiced warfare — he will certainly not be without preparation; this is a hidden stratagem.

units.zh: 且賊兵遠來，利在速戰。
units.en: The rebels have marched far — they need a quick fight.
units.literal: Moreover the rebel troops have come from afar — their advantage lies in swift battle.

units.zh: 今王師自戰其地，利在堅守，不利輕出；
units.en: Our army fights on its own ground — we should hold firm, not sally lightly;
units.literal: Now the imperial army fights on its own ground — the advantage lies in stubborn defense, not in sallying lightly;

units.zh: 若輕出關，是入其算。
units.en: to leave the pass lightly is to fall into their trap.
units.literal: if we lightly leave the pass, we enter their calculation.

units.zh: 乞更觀事勢。」
units.en: I beg to watch the situation longer."
units.literal: I beg to observe the situation further."

units.zh: 楊國忠恐其謀己，屢奏使出兵。
units.en: Yang Guozhong, fearing Han plotted against him, repeatedly urged an advance.
units.literal: Yang Guozhong feared Han plotted against him and repeatedly memorialized to make the army advance.

units.zh: 上久處太平，不練軍事，既為國忠眩惑，中使相繼督責。
units.en: The emperor, long at peace and unused to war, was swayed by Guozhong; palace envoys pressed Han in succession.
units.literal: The emperor had long dwelt in peace and did not practice military affairs; having been dazzled and misled by Guozhong, palace envoys came in succession to supervise and reproach.

units.zh: 翰不得已，引師出關。
units.en: Han had no choice and led the army out.
units.literal: Han had no choice and led the army out of the pass.

units.zh: 六月四日，次於靈寶縣之西原。
units.en: On the fourth of the sixth month they camped on the western plain of Lingbao.
units.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month they halted on the western plain of Lingbao county.

units.zh: 八日，與賊交戰，官軍南迫險峭，北臨黃河；
units.en: On the eighth they fought; the imperial army was pinned south against steep ground and north against the Yellow River;
units.literal: On the eighth day they joined battle with the rebels; the imperial army was pressed on the south by steep peril and faced the Yellow River on the north;

units.zh: 崔乾祐以數千人先據險要。
units.en: Cui Qianyu had seized the heights with several thousand men.
units.literal: Cui Qianyu with several thousand men had first seized the strategic heights.

units.zh: 翰及良丘浮船中流以觀進退，謂乾祐兵少，輕之，遂促將士令進，爭路擁塞，無復隊伍。
units.en: Han and Liangqiu watched from a boat midstream, thought Qianyu's force small, and ordered an advance — the troops jammed the road in disorder.
units.literal: Han and Liangqiu floated a boat midstream to observe advance and retreat; they thought Qianyu's troops few and despised them, then urged the officers and soldiers to advance — they scrambled for the road and jammed together, with no formations left.

units.zh: 午後，東風急，乾祐以草車數十乘縱火焚之，煙焰亙天。
units.en: In the afternoon a strong east wind rose; Qianyu fired dozens of hay carts — smoke filled the sky.
units.literal: In the afternoon the east wind blew hard; Qianyu set fire to several tens of hay carts — smoke and flame filled the sky.

units.zh: 將士掩面，開目不得，因為兇徒所乘，王師自相排擠，墜於河。
units.en: The men could not see for the smoke; the rebels pressed them; the imperial troops trampled one another into the river.
units.literal: Officers and soldiers covered their faces and could not open their eyes; thus they were ridden by the fierce band — the imperial army pushed one another and fell into the river.

units.zh: 其後者見前軍陷敗，悉潰，填委於河，死者數萬人，號叫之聲振天地，縛器械，以槍為楫，投北岸，十不存一二。
units.en: The rear ranks saw the van collapse and fled; tens of thousands drowned in the river, their cries shaking heaven and earth; using spears as oars they tried the north bank — fewer than one in ten survived.
units.literal: Those behind saw the front army trapped and defeated and all fled; they piled into the river — tens of thousands died; cries shook heaven and earth; binding gear and using spears as oars they cast themselves to the north bank — not one or two in ten survived.

units.zh: 軍既敗，翰與數百騎馳而西歸，為火拔歸仁執降於賊。
units.en: Defeated, Han fled west with a few hundred horsemen and was seized by Huoba Guiren and surrendered to the rebels.
units.literal: When the army was defeated, Han with several hundred cavalry galloped west to return and was seized by Huoba Guiren and surrendered to the rebels.

units.zh: 祿山謂之曰：「汝常輕我，今日如何？」
units.en: Lushan said, "You always despised me — how is it today?"
units.literal: Lushan said to him: "You always looked down on me — how is it today?"

units.zh: 翰懼，俯伏稱：「肉眼不識陛下，遂至於此。
units.en: Han prostrated himself in fear and said, "My mortal eyes failed to see Your Majesty, and thus it came to this.
units.literal: Han in fear prostrated himself and said: "These fleshly eyes did not recognize Your Majesty, and thus it came to this.

units.zh: 陛下為撥亂主，今天下未平，李光弼在土門，來填在河南，魯炅在南陽，但留臣，臣以尺書招之，不日平矣。」
units.en: Your Majesty is heaven's chosen restorer; the realm is not yet settled — Li Guangbi holds Tumen, Lai Tian is in Henan, Lu Jiong in Nanyang; keep me and I will summon them by letter, and peace will come in days."
units.literal: Your Majesty is the lord who sets chaos aright; the realm is not yet pacified — Li Guangbi is at Tumen, Lai Tian in Henan, Lu Jiong at Nanyang; only keep your servant — with a short letter your servant will summon them, and in no many days it will be pacified."

units.zh: 祿山大喜，遂偽署翰司空。
units.en: Lushan was delighted and made Han Minister of Works in his false court.
units.literal: Lushan was greatly pleased and thereupon falsely appointed Han Minister of Works.

units.zh: 作書招光弼等，諸將報書皆讓翰不死節。
units.en: He wrote to summon Guangbi and the others; every reply rebuked Han for failing to die with honor.
units.literal: He wrote letters to summon Guangbi and the others; the generals' replies all reproached Han for not dying in honor.

units.zh: 祿山知事不諧，遂閉翰於苑中，潛殺之。
units.en: Lushan saw the plan would fail, imprisoned Han in the park, and had him killed in secret.
units.literal: Lushan knew matters would not work; he then shut Han in the park and secretly killed him.

units.zh: 翰之守潼關也，主天下兵權，肆誌報怨，誣奏戶部尚書安思順與祿山潛通，偽令人為祿山遺思順書，於關門擒之以獻。
units.en: While holding Tong Pass Han wielded imperial military power, indulged revenge, and falsely accused Revenue Minister An Sishun of communicating with Lushan — forging a letter, seizing Sishun at the gate, and presenting him to court.
units.literal: When Han guarded Tong Pass he held command of the empire's military power, indulged his will to avenge grudges, and falsely memorialized that Minister of Revenue An Sishun had secret communication with Lushan — he had someone forge a letter from Lushan to Sishun, seized him at the pass gate, and presented him.

units.zh: 其年三月，思順及弟太仆卿元貞坐誅，徙其家屬於嶺外，天下冤之。
units.en: That third month Sishun and his brother Yuanzhen, Grand Master of the Stud, were executed and their families exiled beyond the Ling ranges — the realm judged it a gross injustice.
units.literal: In the third month of that year Sishun and his younger brother Grand Master of the Stud Yuanzhen were executed on conviction; their families were moved beyond the Ling ranges — the realm considered it unjust.

units.zh: 史臣曰：大盜作梗，祿山亂常，詞雖欲誅國忠，誌則謀危社稷。
units.en: Commentary. The historiographer writes: The great rebel rose; Lushan overturned the order — he spoke of punishing Guozhong but aimed at the throne itself.
units.literal: Commentary. The historiographer says: The great bandit raised obstruction; Lushan disturbed the norms — in words he wished to execute Guozhong, but in intent he plotted to endanger the altars of state.

units.zh: 於時承平日久，金革道消，封常清、高仙芝相次率不教之兵，募市人之眾，以抗AT寇，失律喪師。
units.en: Peace had lasted so long that warcraft had faded; Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi in turn led untrained troops and market rabble against the rebels — and lost their armies.
units.literal: At that time peace had lasted long and the way of arms and armor had faded; Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi in succession led untrained troops and recruited crowds of market folk to resist the rebel band — they lost discipline and lost their armies.

units.zh: 哥舒翰廢疾於家，起專兵柄，二十萬眾拒賊關門，軍中之務不親，委任又非其所。
units.en: Ge Shuhan, invalid at home, was raised to sole command; two hundred thousand held the pass — yet he did not lead in person and his deputies were unfit.
units.literal: Ge Shuhan, disabled by illness at home, was raised to monopolize military power; two hundred thousand resisted the rebels at the pass gate — he did not personally handle army affairs, and those entrusted were not fit for their posts.

units.zh: 及遇羯賊，旋致敗亡，天子以之播遷，自身以之拘執，此皆命帥而不得其人也。
units.en: They met the rebels and were swiftly destroyed — the emperor fled, they were captured — all because the wrong men were given command.
units.literal: When they met the Jie rebels they quickly met defeat and ruin — the Son of Heaven was driven to wander, they themselves were seized and held — all this from appointing commanders and not getting the right men.

units.zh: 《禮》曰：「大夫死眾。」
units.en: The Rites says, "A grandee dies for the multitude."
units.literal: The Rites says: "A grandee dies for the multitude."

units.zh: 又曰：「謀人之軍師敗則死之。」
units.en: It also says, "The strategist who fails must die."
units.literal: It also says: "One who plots as another's military adviser — if defeated, dies for it."

units.zh: 翰受署賊庭，茍延視息，忠義之道，即可知也，豈不愧於顏杲卿乎！
units.en: Han took office under the rebels and clung to life — his loyalty is plain; how could he not blush before Yan Gaoqing!
units.literal: Han accepted appointment in the rebel court and clung to life drawing breath — the way of loyalty and righteousness can be known from this; how is he not ashamed before Yan Gaoqing!

units.zh: 抑又聞之，古之命將者，推轂而謂之曰：「閫外之事，將軍裁之。」
units.en: We also hear that ancient emperors, appointing a general, would push the chariot wheel and say, "Beyond the gate, the general decides."
units.literal: Moreover it is heard that in antiquity when appointing generals, they would push the chariot wheel and say: "Matters outside the gate — the general decides."

units.zh: 觀楊國忠之奏事，邊令誠之護戎，又掣肘於軍政者也，未可偏責三帥，不尤伊人。
units.en: Consider Yang Guozhong's interference and Bian Lingcheng's supervision — the court hamstrung its generals; one cannot blame the three commanders alone.
units.literal: Considering Yang Guozhong's memorials, Bian Lingcheng's supervision of the army — again hamstringing military affairs — one cannot lay all blame on the three commanders alone or reproach those men only.

units.zh: 後之君子，得不深鑒！
units.en: Let later ages take this deeply to heart!
units.literal: Gentlemen of later ages — can they not take this as a deep mirror!

units.zh: 贊曰：羯賊犯順，戎車啟行。
units.en: Praise runs: The Jie rebels rose in treason; war chariots rolled out.
units.literal: The praise says: The Jie rebels violated obedience; war chariots set out.

units.zh: 委任失所，封、高敗亡。
units.en: Wrong men were chosen — Feng and Gao were destroyed.
units.literal: Appointments lost their place — Feng and Gao were defeated and perished.

units.zh: 虔劉圻甸，僭竊衣裳。
units.en: They ravaged the heartland and stole the imperial robes.
units.literal: They slaughtered the capital region and usurped the imperial robes.

units.zh: 醜哉舒翰，不能死王。
units.en: Shame on Shuhan, who could not die for his sovereign.
units.literal: Shameful is Shuhan — he could not die for his lord.

units.zh: 魯炅，范陽人也。
units.en: Lu Jiong was from Fanyang.
units.literal: Lu Jiong—Lu Jiong was a native of Fanyang.

units.zh: 炅時立在階下，翰指炅曰：「此人後當為節度使矣。」
units.en: Jiong was standing on the steps below. Han pointed to him and said, "This man will one day be a military governor."
units.literal: Jiong was then standing below the steps; Han pointed at Jiong and said, "This man will later become a military governor."

units.zh: 天寶六年，隴右節度使哥舒翰引為別奏。
units.en: In the sixth year of Tianbao, Geshu Han, military governor of Longyou, brought him in as a special memorialist.
units.literal: the Longyou military governor Geshu Han recruited him as a special memorialist.

units.zh: 十五載正月，拜炅上洛太守，未行，遷南陽太守、本郡守捉，仍充防禦使。
units.en: In the first month of the fifteenth year, Jiong was named Governor of Shangluo. Before he departed, he was moved to Governor of Nanyang with local defense duties and made defense commissioner as well.
units.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year, Jiong was appointed Governor of Shangluo; before he set out, he was transferred to Governor of Nanyang, with charge of defending his own prefecture, and was also made defense commissioner.

units.zh: 尋兼御史大夫，充南陽節度使，以嶺南、黔中、山南東道子弟五萬人屯葉縣北，滍水之南，築柵，四面掘壕以自固。
units.en: He was soon given the concurrent title Censor-in-Chief and made Nanyang military governor. He stationed fifty thousand troops from Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Shannan East north of Ye County and south of the Zhi River, built stockades, and dug trenches on every side to hold his position.
units.literal: Soon he was also made Censor-in-Chief and Nanyang military governor; with fifty thousand youths from Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Shannan East Circuit he encamped north of Ye County and south of the Zhi River, built palisades, and dug moats on all sides to fortify himself.

units.zh: 賊又知其決死，遂不敢逼，朝廷因除御史大夫、襄陽節度使。
units.en: Seeing their willingness to die to the last man, the rebels dared not close in. The court then appointed him Censor-in-Chief and military governor of Xiangyang.
units.literal: The rebels again knew their resolve to die and did not press them; the court thereupon appointed him Censor-in-Chief and Xiangyang military governor.

units.zh: 後以隴右破吐蕃跳蕩功，累授右領軍大將軍同正員，賜紫金魚袋。
units.en: Later, for victories over Tibetan raiders in Longyou, he rose step by step to Right Army General-in-Chief with full concurrent rank and received the purple-gold fish tally.
units.literal: Later, for merit in defeating the Tibetan raiders in Longyou, he was repeatedly promoted to Right Army General-in-Chief with concurrent status and was granted the purple-gold fish tally.

units.zh: 身長七尺餘，涉獵書史，
units.en: He was over seven chi tall and had read widely in history and the classics.
units.literal: He stood more than seven chi in height and had dipped into books and histories,

units.zh: 至五月，賊將武令珣、畢思琛等來擊之，眾欲出戰，炅不許。
units.en: In the fifth month, rebel generals Wu Lingxun and Bi Sichen attacked. The men wanted to give battle, but Jiong refused.
units.literal: By the fifth month, the rebel generals Wu Lingxun, Bi Sichen, and others came to attack; the troops wished to go out and fight, but Jiong would not allow it.

units.zh: 賊於營西順風燒煙，營內坐立不得，橫門扇及木爭出，賊矢集如雨，炅與中使薛道等挺身遁走，余眾盡沒。
units.en: The rebels set smoke to windward west of the camp until the troops could neither sit nor stand. They surged through the side gates and over the timbers; arrows fell like rain. Jiong, the palace envoy Xue Dao, and others bolted, and the remainder of the army was destroyed.
units.literal: The rebels burned smoke upwind on the west of the camp; inside the camp men could neither sit nor stand; they rushed the side gates and timbers to get out; rebel arrows fell like rain; Jiong, the palace envoy Xue Dao, and others fled headlong, and the rest of the force was wiped out.

units.zh: 炅收合殘卒，保南陽郡，為賊所圍。
units.en: Jiong rallied the survivors, held Nanyang, and was surrounded by the rebels.
units.literal: Jiong gathered the broken remnants and held Nanyang Prefecture, and was besieged by the rebels.

units.zh: 炅在圍中一年，救兵不至，晝夜苦戰，人相食。
units.en: Jiong remained under siege for a year. No relief arrived. Day and night the fighting was desperate, and men ate one another.
units.literal: Jiong was besieged for a year; relief did not come; day and night they fought bitterly; men ate one another.

units.zh: 尋而潼關失守，賊使哥舒翰招之，不從。
units.en: Soon after Tong Pass fell, the rebels sent Geshu Han to win him over, but he refused.
units.literal: Before long Tong Pass fell; the rebels sent Geshu Han to summon him, but he would not submit.

units.zh: 又使偽將豫州刺史武令珣等攻之，累月不能克。
units.en: They then sent the puppet Yuzhou prefect Wu Lingxun and others against him; for months they could not capture the city.
units.literal: They again sent the false general and Yuzhou prefect Wu Lingxun and others to attack him; for many months they could not take the city.

units.zh: 武令珣死，又令田承嗣攻之。
units.en: After Wu Lingxun died, Tian Chengsi was ordered to press the siege.
units.literal: When Wu Lingxun died, they ordered Tian Chengsi to attack.

units.zh: 炅城中食盡，煮牛皮筋角而食之，米鬥至四五十千，有價無米，鼠一頭至四百文，餓死者相枕藉。
units.en: Provisions in the city ran out. The defenders boiled ox hide, sinew, and horn to eat. A dou of rice cost forty or fifty thousand cash—money without grain to buy. A rat sold for four hundred cash. The dead from hunger lay heaped together.
units.literal: Food in Jiong's city was exhausted; they boiled ox hide, sinew, and horn to eat; a dou of rice reached forty or fifty thousand cash—there was a price but no grain; a single rat fetched four hundred cash; the starved lay piled one upon another.

units.zh: 至德二年五月十五日，率眾持滿傳矢突圍而出南陽，投襄陽。
units.en: In the second year of Zhide, on the fifteenth of the fifth month he led his men, bows fully drawn and arrows at the ready, in a breakout from Nanyang and made for Xiangyang.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhide, on the fifteenth day of the fifth month he led the masses, bows strung and arrows passed along, to burst the encirclement and break out of Nanyang, and threw himself on Xiangyang.

units.zh: 田承嗣來追，苦戰二日，殺賊甚眾。
units.en: Tian Chengsi pursued. For two days they fought fiercely and killed a great many rebels.
units.literal: Tian Chengsi came in pursuit; for two days they fought bitterly and killed many rebels.

units.zh: 時賊志欲南侵江、漢，賴炅奮命扼其沖要，南夏所以保全。
units.en: The rebels then meant to drive south into the Yangzi and Han valleys. Jiong's desperate stand at the vital pass is what kept the south intact.
units.literal: At that time the rebels intended to push south into the Yangzi and Han regions; it was by Jiong's desperate defense of the strategic choke point that South China was preserved.

units.zh: 日昇既入城，炅眾初以為望絕，忽有使來宣命，皆踴躍一心。
units.en: When Risheng entered the city, Jiong's men had thought themselves forsaken. Suddenly an envoy arrived with the imperial message, and they rallied as one.
units.literal: Once Risheng had entered the city, Jiong's troops had at first thought all hope gone; suddenly an envoy came bearing the imperial charge, and all leapt up with one heart.

units.zh: 大將管崇嗣於行在朝堂背闕而坐，言笑自若，勉劾之，拘於有司，肅宗特原之，歎曰：「吾有李勉，始知朝廷尊也。」
units.en: The general Guan Congsi sat in the mobile court's audience hall with his back to the throne, chatting and laughing as though unconcerned. Mian impeached him and had him held by the proper authorities. Emperor Suzong personally pardoned Guan and sighed, "Only with Li Mian do I learn that the court commands respect."
units.literal: The great general Guan Congsi at the mobile court sat in the audience hall with his back to the imperial presence, talking and laughing as if at ease; Mian impeached him and had him detained by the appropriate office; Suzong specially pardoned him and sighed, saying, "With Li Mian, I now know that the court is honored."

units.zh: 無何，邕管黃家賊叛，詔象古發兵數道共討之，像古命清領兵三千赴焉。
units.en: Before long, the Huang bandits rebelled in Yong and Guan. The court ordered Li Xianggu to attack on several fronts. Li Xianggu sent Yang Qing with three thousand men to join the campaign.
units.literal: Before long, Huang bandits rebelled in Yong and Guan; an edict ordered Xianggu to dispatch troops on several routes jointly to suppress them; Xianggu ordered Qing to lead three thousand troops to go there.

units.zh: 及渭上軍破，賊將崔乾祐先鎮蒲、同，使麾下騎三十人捉器，器遂北走靈武。
units.en: When the Wei River force was broken, the rebel general Cui Qianyou—already holding Pu and Tong—sent thirty horsemen to seize Qi, and Qi fled north to Lingwu.
units.literal: When the Wei River army was defeated, the rebel general Cui Qianyou, who was already garrisoning Pu and Tong prefectures, sent thirty horsemen under his command to seize Qi; Qi fled north to Lingwu.

units.zh: 逆胡陷西京．器沒於賊，仍守奉先。
units.en: When the rebel armies seized the Western Capital, Qi was caught in occupied territory yet continued to govern Fengxian.
units.literal: When the rebel barbarian took the Western Capital, Qi fell into the rebels' hands but continued to hold Fengxian.
